title.zh: 卷五十八 志第三十九: 百官四 符制 印製 鐵券 官誥 百官俸給
title.en: Volume 58 Treatises 39: Official Posts 4: Counting Systems, Printing, Iron Certificates, Official Proclamations, Official Salaries
title.raw: 卷五十八 志第三十九: 百官四 符制 印製 鐵券 官誥 百官俸給 Volume 58 Treatises 39: Official Posts 4: Counting Systems, Printing, Iron Certificates, Official Proclamations, Official Salaries

sentences.zh: 初，穆宗之前，諸部長各刻信牌，交互馳驛，訊事擾人。

translations.literal: In the beginning, before Emperor Muzong, each tribal chief carved his own credential tally; they dispatched relay riders back and forth to investigate matters, disturbing the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the early days, before the reign of Emperor Muzong, each tribal chief carved his own travel tally and sent relay riders back and forth on inquiries, harassing the populace.

sentences.zh: 太祖獻議，自非穆宗之命，擅制牌號者置重法。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu offered a proposal: except by order of Muzong, those who presumptuously made tallies and insignia should be subjected to severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu proposed that anyone who presumptuously made tallies or insignia without Muzong's authorization should face severe penalties.

sentences.zh: 自是，號令始一。

translations.literal: From this time, commands began to be unified.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, imperial commands were finally unified.

sentences.zh: 收國二年九月，始制金牌，後又有銀牌、木牌之制。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of Shouguo year 2, gold tallies were first instituted; later there were also regulations for silver tallies and wooden tallies.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of Shouguo (1116), the gold tally was instituted; silver and wooden tallies were added later.

sentences.zh: 蓋金牌以授萬戶，銀牌以授猛安，木牌則謀克、蒲輦所佩者也。

translations.literal: Generally, gold tallies were conferred on wanhu, silver tallies on meng'an, and wooden tallies were worn by mouke and puyan.
translations.idiomatic: Gold tallies went to wanhu commanders, silver tallies to meng'an, and wooden tallies were worn by mouke and puyan officers.

sentences.zh: 故國初與空名宣頭付軍帥，以為功賞。

translations.literal: Therefore in the founding of the state, honorary appointment edicts with blank names were given to military commanders as rewards for merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty, blank appointment edicts were issued to military commanders as rewards for distinguished service.

sentences.zh: 遞牌，即國初之信牌也。

translations.literal: Dispatch tallies were the credential tallies of the founding of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch tallies were simply the credential tallies used at the dynasty's founding.

sentences.zh: 至皇統五年三月，複更造金銀牌，其制皆不傳。

translations.literal: By the third month of Huangtong year 5, gold and silver tallies were again newly made, but their specifications are no longer transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year of Huangtong (1145), gold and silver tallies were reissued, though their specifications have not survived.

sentences.zh: 大定二十九年，制綠油紅字者，尚書省文字省遞用之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Dading, those with green lacquer and red characters were instituted; documents of the Secretariat used provincial dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Dading (1189), a green-lacquer, red-character tally was established for provincial dispatch of Secretariat documents.

sentences.zh: 硃漆金字者，敕遞用之。

translations.literal: Those with cinnabar lacquer and gold characters were used for imperial-edict dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Cinnabar-lacquer tallies with gold characters were used for imperial-edict dispatch.

sentences.zh: 並左右司掌之，有合遞文字，則牌送各部，付馬鋪轉遞，日行二百五十裏。

translations.literal: Both were managed by the Left and Right Bureaus; when there were documents to be dispatched, the tally was sent to each department, handed to relay stations for transfer dispatch, traveling two hundred fifty li per day.
translations.idiomatic: Both types were kept by the Left and Right Bureaus of the Secretariat. When documents required dispatch, a tally was sent to each department and handed to relay stations for transfer, at a rate of two hundred fifty li per day.

sentences.zh: 如台部別奉聖旨文字，亦給如上制。

translations.literal: If the Censorate separately presented memorial documents bearing imperial rescripts, they too were issued according to the above regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Documents bearing separate imperial rescripts from the Censorate were issued under the same regulations.

sentences.zh: 虎符之制，承安元年制。

translations.literal: The system of tiger tallies was instituted in the first year of Chengan.
translations.idiomatic: The tiger-tally system was established in the first year of Chengan (1196).

sentences.zh: 以禮官言，漢與郡國守相為銅虎符，唐以銅魚符，起軍旅、易守長等用之。

translations.literal: According to the ceremonial officials, the Han divided bronze tiger tallies with prefectural and commandery governors; the Tang used bronze fish tallies — these were used to raise armies, replace local administrators, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial officials noted that the Han used paired bronze tiger tallies shared with commandery and prefecture administrators, while the Tang used bronze fish tallies for mobilizing troops, replacing local officials, and similar purposes.

sentences.zh: 至是，斟酌漢、唐典故，其符用虎，並五左一右，左者留御前，以侍臣親密者掌之，其右付隨路統軍司、招討司長官主之，闕則次官主之。

translations.literal: At this time, drawing on Han and Tang precedents, the tally took the form of a tiger; altogether there were five left halves and one right half. The left halves were kept before the throne and held by trusted intimate attendants; the right half was entrusted to the chief officers of the Regional Military Commands and Pacification Commissions along each route — if absent, the deputy officer held it.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on Han and Tang precedents, the Jin adopted a tiger-shaped tally in sets of five left halves and one right half. The left halves remained at court in the custody of trusted intimate attendants; the right half was held by the senior officer of each route's Regional Military Command or Pacification Commission, or by the deputy in his absence.

sentences.zh: 若發兵三百人以上及徵兵、召易本司長貳官，從尚書省奏請左第一符，近侍局以囊封付主奏者，尚書備錄聖旨，與符以函同封，用尚書省印記之，皆專使帶牌馳送至彼。

translations.literal: If mobilizing three hundred or more troops, or conscripting soldiers, or summoning and replacing the chief and deputy officers of a bureau, the request would proceed from the Secretariat for the first left tally; the Inner Service Bureau would seal it in a pouch and give it to the chief petitioner; the Secretariat would record the imperial rescript, seal the tally together with it in a case, affix the Secretariat seal, and all were sent by special messenger bearing the tally at full relay speed to the destination.
translations.idiomatic: To mobilize three hundred or more troops, conscript soldiers, or summon and replace the chief and deputy officers of a bureau, the Secretariat would request the first left tally. The Inner Service Bureau sealed it in a pouch and delivered it to the chief petitioner; the Secretariat recorded the imperial rescript, placed the tally in a case with it, affixed the Secretariat seal, and dispatched a special messenger bearing the tally at full relay speed.

sentences.zh: 主符者視其封，以右符勘合，然後奉行，若一有參差者，不敢承用。

translations.literal: The holder of the tally would examine its seal, verify it against the right tally, and only then execute it; if there was any discrepancy, he would not dare accept and use it.
translations.idiomatic: The officer holding the tally examined the seal and verified it against the right half before acting on the order; if anything did not match, he dared not accept it.

sentences.zh: 主者複用囊封貯左符，上用職印，具發兵狀與符以本司印封，即日還付使者，送尚書省以進，乃更其封，以付內掌之人。

translations.literal: The holder would again use a pouch to store the left tally, affix his office seal on top, prepare a mobilization report and seal the tally with his bureau's seal, return it the same day to the messenger, who would deliver it to the Secretariat for presentation; then the seal would be changed and it would be given to the inner custodian.
translations.idiomatic: The receiving officer resealed the left tally in a pouch, affixed his office seal, prepared a mobilization report, and sealed both report and tally with his bureau's seal. He returned them the same day to the messenger, who delivered them to the Secretariat; the seal was then changed and the tally restored to its inner custodian.

sentences.zh: 若複有事，左符以次出，周而復始，仍各置曆注付受日月。

translations.literal: If there was further business, the left tallies were issued in sequence, cycling through again and again; registers were kept recording the dates of receipt and delivery.
translations.idiomatic: When further orders arose, the left tallies were issued in rotation, cycling through the set again and again, with registers recording the dates of each transfer.

sentences.zh: 若盜賊急速不容先陳者，雖三百人以上，其掌兵官司亦許給付，隨即言上，詔即施行之。

translations.literal: If bandits were urgent and there was no time to report first, even for three hundred or more troops, the bureau in charge of troops was also permitted to grant and issue; it would immediately report upward, and the edict took effect at once.
translations.idiomatic: In emergencies involving bandits when there was no time to report first, even for mobilizations of three hundred or more, the bureau in charge of troops was permitted to issue the tally immediately and report afterward; the order took effect at once.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年，更定樞密院用鹿符，宣撫司用魚符，統軍司用虎符。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyou, it was revised that the Privy Council would use deer tallies, Pacification Commissions fish tallies, and Regional Military Commands tiger tallies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyou (1215), new rules assigned deer tallies to the Privy Council, fish tallies to Pacification Commissions, and tiger tallies to Regional Military Commands.

sentences.zh: 若發銀牌，若省付部及點檢司者，左右司用匣封印，驗封交受。

translations.literal: When issuing silver tallies, if dispatched from the Secretariat to a department or the Inspection Bureau, the Left and Right Bureaus used a sealed case; the seal was verified upon receipt and delivery.
translations.idiomatic: When silver tallies were dispatched from the Secretariat to a department or the Inspection Bureau, the Left and Right Bureaus sealed them in a case and verified the seal upon receipt.

sentences.zh: 若發於他處，並封題押，以匣貯之。

translations.literal: If dispatched elsewhere, all were sealed, labeled, and stored in a case.
translations.idiomatic: When dispatched elsewhere, they were sealed, labeled, and stored in a case.

sentences.zh: 太子之寶。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent's Seal.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Apparent's Seal.

sentences.zh: 大定二十二年，世宗幸上京。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Dading, Emperor Shizong visited Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Dading (1182), Emperor Shizong visited Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 鑄「守國之寶」以授皇太子。

translations.literal: He cast the "Seal for Guarding the Realm" and bestowed it on the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He cast the Seal for Guarding the Realm and bestowed it on the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，世宗不豫，以皇太孫攝政，鑄「攝政之寶」。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, Emperor Shizong fell ill; the Imperial Grandson served as regent, and the "Regency Seal" was cast.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year (1188), when Emperor Shizong fell ill, the Imperial Grandson served as regent and the Regency Seal was cast.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年十二月，以皇太子守緒控制樞密院，詔以金鑄「撫軍之寶」，如世宗時制，於啟稟之際用之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Zhenyou, as Crown Prince Shouxu controlled the Privy Council, an edict ordered the gold-casting of the "Seal for Pacifying the Army," following Emperor Shizong's precedent, to be used when presenting reports.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year of Zhenyou (1215), Crown Prince Shouxu was placed in charge of the Privy Council. An edict ordered a gold Seal for Pacifying the Army cast, following Emperor Shizong's precedent, for use when presenting reports to the throne.

sentences.zh: 百官之印。

translations.literal: Seals of the Hundred Officials.
translations.idiomatic: Seals of the Hundred Officials.

sentences.zh: 天會六年，始詔給諸司，其前所帶印記無問有無新給，悉上送官，敢匿者國有常憲。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhui, an edict was first issued granting seals to all bureaus; previously held seals, whether old or newly issued, were all to be surrendered to the government; those who dared conceal them were subject to statutory punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhui (1128), an edict first granted official seals to all bureaus. All previously held seals, whether old or newly issued, had to be surrendered; concealment was punishable under statute.

sentences.zh: 至正隆元年，以內外官印新舊名及階品大小不一，有用遼、宋舊印及契丹字者，遂定制，命禮部更鑄焉。

translations.literal: By the first year of Zhenglong, because internal and external official seals had inconsistent old and new names and ranks of varying sizes, and some used old Liao and Song seals and Khitan script, regulations were therefore established and the Ministry of Rites was ordered to recast them.
translations.idiomatic: By the first year of Zhenglong (1156), official seals inside and outside the capital bore inconsistent names and ranks of varying sizes; some still used old Liao and Song seals or Khitan script. Standard regulations were therefore established and the Ministry of Rites ordered to recast all seals.

sentences.zh: 三師、三公、親王、尚書令並金印，方二寸，重八十兩，駝紐。

translations.literal: The Three Preceptors, Three Dukes, Princes, and Director of the Department all received gold seals, square two cun, weighing eighty liang, with camel-shaped knobs.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Preceptors, Three Dukes, Princes, and Director of the Department all received gold seals two cun square, weighing eighty liang, with camel-shaped knobs.

sentences.zh: 一字王印，方一寸七分半，金鍍銀， 重四十兩，鍍金三字。

translations.literal: Princes with single-character titles received seals square one cun seven fen and a half, silver gilt with gold, weighing forty liang, with three characters gilt in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Princes with single-character titles received seals one cun and seven and a half fen square, of gilt silver weighing forty liang, with three gilt-gold characters.

sentences.zh: 諸郡王印，方一寸六分半，金鍍銀，重三十五兩，鍍金三字。

translations.literal: Seals of various commandery princes were square one cun six fen and a half, silver gilt with gold, weighing thirty-five liang, with three characters gilt in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery princes received seals one cun and six and a half fen square, of gilt silver weighing thirty-five liang, with three gilt-gold characters.

sentences.zh: 國公無印。

translations.literal: State Dukes had no seal.
translations.idiomatic: State Dukes received no seal.

sentences.zh: 一品印，方一寸六分半，金鍍銀，重三十五兩，鍍金三字。

translations.literal: First-rank seals were square one cun six fen and a half, silver gilt with gold, weighing thirty-five liang, with three characters gilt in gold.
translations.idiomatic: First-rank seals were one cun and six and a half fen square, of gilt silver weighing thirty-five liang, with three gilt-gold characters.

sentences.zh: 二品印，方一寸六分，金鍍銅，重二十六兩。

translations.literal: Second-rank seals were square one cun six fen, copper gilt with gold, weighing twenty-six liang.
translations.idiomatic: Second-rank seals were one cun and six fen square, of gilt copper weighing twenty-six liang.

sentences.zh: 東宮三師、宰執與郡王同。

translations.literal: The Three Preceptors of the Eastern Palace and chief ministers were the same as commandery princes.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Preceptors of the Eastern Palace and chief ministers received the same seals as commandery princes.

sentences.zh: 三品印，方一寸五分半，銅，重二十四兩。

translations.literal: Third-rank seals were square one cun five fen and a half, copper, weighing twenty-four liang.
translations.idiomatic: Third-rank seals were one cun and five and a half fen square, of copper weighing twenty-four liang.

sentences.zh: 四品印，方一寸五分，銅，重二十兩。

translations.literal: Fourth-rank seals were square one cun five fen, copper, weighing twenty liang.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth-rank seals were one cun and five fen square, of copper weighing twenty liang.

sentences.zh: 五品印，方一寸四分，銅，重二十兩。

translations.literal: Fifth-rank seals were square one cun four fen, copper, weighing twenty liang.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth-rank seals were one cun and four fen square, of copper weighing twenty liang.

sentences.zh: 六品印，一寸三分，銅，重十六兩。

translations.literal: Sixth-rank seals were one cun three fen, copper, weighing sixteen liang.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth-rank seals were one cun and three fen square, of copper weighing sixteen liang.

sentences.zh: 七品印，一寸二分，銅，重十六兩。

translations.literal: Seventh-rank seals were one cun two fen, copper, weighing sixteen liang.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh-rank seals were one cun and two fen square, of copper weighing sixteen liang.

sentences.zh: 八品印，一寸一分半，銅，重十四兩。

translations.literal: Eighth-rank seals were one cun one fen and a half, copper, weighing fourteen liang.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth-rank seals were one cun and one and a half fen square, of copper weighing fourteen liang.

sentences.zh: 九品印，一寸一分，銅，重十四兩。

translations.literal: Ninth-rank seals were one cun one fen, copper, weighing fourteen liang.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth-rank seals were one cun and one fen square, of copper weighing fourteen liang.

sentences.zh: 凡硃記，方一寸，銅，重十四兩。

translations.literal: All vermillion seals were square one cun, copper, weighing fourteen liang.
translations.idiomatic: All secondary vermillion seals were one cun square, of copper weighing fourteen liang.

sentences.zh: 以鐵為之，狀如卷瓦。

translations.literal: It was made of iron, shaped like a curved roof tile.
translations.idiomatic: It was made of iron, shaped like a curved roof tile.

sentences.zh: 刻字畫襴，以金填之。

translations.literal: Characters and decorative patterns were carved, filled in with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Characters and decorative patterns were carved and inlaid with gold.

sentences.zh: 外以禦寶為合，半留內府，以賞殊功也。

translations.literal: On the outside the imperial seal served as the cover; half was kept in the inner palace, to reward exceptional merit.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial seal served as the outer cover; half the certificate was kept in the inner palace, to reward exceptional merit.

sentences.zh: 親王，紅遍地雲氣翔鸞錦褾，金鸞五色羅十五幅，寶裝犀軸。

translations.literal: Princes: red ground brocade mounting with cloud motifs and soaring phoenixes, fifteen panels of five-colored silk with gold phoenixes, scroll rod of rhinoceros horn with jeweled fittings.
translations.idiomatic: Princes received patents with red-ground brocade borders featuring clouds and soaring phoenixes, fifteen panels of five-colored silk with gold phoenixes, and a jeweled rhinoceros-horn scroll rod.

sentences.zh: 一品，紅遍地雲鶴錦褾，金雲鶴五色羅十四幅，犀軸。

translations.literal: First rank: red ground brocade mounting with cloud cranes, fourteen panels of five-colored silk with gold cloud cranes, rhinoceros-horn scroll rod.
translations.idiomatic: First rank: red-ground brocade borders with cloud cranes, fourteen panels of five-colored silk with gold cloud cranes, and a rhinoceros-horn scroll rod.

sentences.zh: 二品、三品，紅遍地龜蓮錦褾，素五色綾十二幅，玳瑁軸。

translations.literal: Second and third ranks: red ground brocade mounting with tortoise and lotus, twelve panels of plain five-colored damask, tortoiseshell scroll rod.
translations.idiomatic: Second and third ranks: red-ground brocade borders with tortoise and lotus motifs, twelve panels of plain five-colored damask, and a tortoiseshell scroll rod.

sentences.zh: 四品、五品，紅遍地水藻戲鱗錦褾，大白綾十幅，銀里間鍍軸，元牙軸承安四年改之，大安二年複改為金縷角軸。

translations.literal: Fourth and fifth ranks: red ground brocade mounting with water plants and sporting fish scales, ten panels of large white damask, scroll rod with silver inlay and gilt fittings; originally ivory scroll rods, changed in the fourth year of Chengan, and in the second year of Da'an again changed to gold-threaded horn scroll rods.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth and fifth ranks: red-ground brocade borders with water plants and fish scales, ten panels of large white damask, and a scroll rod with silver inlay and gilt fittings. Ivory rods were replaced in the fourth year of Chengan (1199), and in the second year of Da'an (1210) gold-threaded horn rods were adopted.

sentences.zh: 六品、七品，紅遍地草錦褾，小白綾八幅，角軸，大安加銀縷。

translations.literal: Sixth and seventh ranks: red ground brocade mounting with grass pattern, eight panels of small white damask, horn scroll rod; in Da'an silver threading was added.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth and seventh ranks: red-ground brocade borders with grass motifs, eight panels of small white damask, and horn scroll rods; silver threading was added in Da'an.

sentences.zh: 公主、王妃與親王同。

translations.literal: Imperial princesses and princess consorts were the same as princes.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princesses and princess consorts received the same patents as princes.

sentences.zh: 郡主、縣主、夫人，紅遍地瑞蓮鸂鶒錦褾，金蓮鸂鶒五色羅十五幅。

translations.literal: Commandery ladies, county ladies, and Ladies: red ground brocade mounting with auspicious lotus and mandarin duck motifs, fifteen panels of five-colored silk with gold lotus and mandarin ducks.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery ladies, county ladies, and Ladies received red-ground brocade borders with auspicious lotus and mandarin duck motifs, and fifteen panels of five-colored silk with gold lotus and mandarin ducks.

sentences.zh: 郡王夫人、國夫人，紅遍地芙蓉花錦褾，金花五色綾十二幅，玳瑁軸。

translations.literal: Consorts of commandery princes and State Ladies: red ground brocade mounting with hibiscus flowers, twelve panels of five-colored damask with gold flowers, tortoiseshell scroll rod.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts of commandery princes and State Ladies received red-ground brocade borders with hibiscus flowers, twelve panels of five-colored damask with gold flowers, and tortoiseshell scroll rods.

sentences.zh: 縣君、孺人、鄉君，紅遍地雜花錦褾，素五色小綾十幅，銀里間鍍軸。

translations.literal: County ladies, Ruren, and Township ladies: red ground brocade mounting with mixed flowers, ten panels of plain small five-colored damask, scroll rod with silver inlay and gilt fittings.
translations.idiomatic: County ladies, Ruren, and Township ladies received red-ground brocade borders with mixed floral motifs, ten panels of plain small five-colored damask, and scroll rods with silver inlay and gilt fittings.

sentences.zh: 軸之制，如徑二寸餘大錢貫樞之，兩端複以犀象為鈿以轄之，可圓轉如輪。

translations.literal: The design of the scroll rod was like stringing large coins of more than two cun in diameter on an axle; both ends were further fitted with rhinoceros and ivory ornaments as caps to secure them, able to rotate round like a wheel.
translations.idiomatic: Scroll rods were fashioned like an axle strung with large coins over two cun in diameter; rhinoceros and ivory caps secured both ends, allowing the rod to rotate freely like a wheel.

sentences.zh: 金格，一品，紅羅畫雲氣盤龍錦褾，金龍五色羅十七幅，寶裝玉軸。

translations.literal: Gold-bound patents: first rank, red silk with painted cloud motifs and coiled dragons brocade mounting, seventeen panels of five-colored silk with gold dragons, jade scroll rod with jeweled fittings.
translations.idiomatic: Gold-bound patents for first rank: red silk with cloud and coiled-dragon brocade borders, seventeen panels of five-colored silk with gold dragons, and a jeweled jade scroll rod.

sentences.zh: 二品，翔鳳褾，金鳳羅十六幅，犀軸。

translations.literal: Second rank: soaring phoenix mounting, sixteen panels of silk with gold phoenixes, rhinoceros-horn scroll rod.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank: soaring-phoenix borders, sixteen panels of silk with gold phoenixes, and a rhinoceros-horn scroll rod.

sentences.zh: 三品、四品，盤鳳褾，金鳳羅十五幅。

translations.literal: Third and fourth ranks: coiled phoenix mounting, fifteen panels of silk with gold phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Third and fourth ranks: coiled-phoenix borders and fifteen panels of silk with gold phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 五品，翔鸞錦褾，金鸞羅十四幅。

translations.literal: Fifth rank: soaring luan brocade mounting, fourteen panels of silk with gold luan.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank: soaring-luan brocade borders and fourteen panels of silk with gold luan birds.

sentences.zh: 以上幅皆用五色羅，軸皆用犀。

translations.literal: For all the above, the panels all used five-colored silk, and the scroll rods all used rhinoceros horn.
translations.idiomatic: For all ranks above, the panels were of five-colored silk and the scroll rods of rhinoceros horn.

sentences.zh: 六品，禦仙花錦褾，金花五色綾十二幅。

translations.literal: Sixth rank: imperial immortal flower brocade mounting, twelve panels of five-colored damask with gold flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank: imperial immortal-flower brocade borders and twelve panels of five-colored damask with gold flowers.

sentences.zh: 七品、八品、九品，太平花錦褾，金花五色小綾十幅。

translations.literal: Seventh, eighth, and ninth ranks: great peace flower brocade mounting, ten panels of small five-colored damask with gold flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, eighth, and ninth ranks: great-peace-flower brocade borders and ten panels of small five-colored damask with gold flowers.

sentences.zh: 軸皆用玳瑁。

translations.literal: The scroll rods all used tortoiseshell.
translations.idiomatic: Their scroll rods were all of tortoiseshell.

sentences.zh: 凡褾皆紅，幅皆五色。

translations.literal: All mountings were red; all panels were five-colored.
translations.idiomatic: All borders were red and all panels five-colored.

sentences.zh: 夫人以上制授，餘敕授，皆給本色錦囊。

translations.literal: Those of Lady rank and above were conferred by formal decree; the rest by imperial command — all were given matching brocade pouches.
translations.idiomatic: Patents for Ladies and above were conferred by formal decree; lower ranks received them by imperial command. All were given matching brocade pouches.

sentences.zh: 百官俸給

translations.literal: Official Salaries of the Hundred Officials.
translations.idiomatic: Official Salaries.

sentences.zh: 正一品：三師，錢粟三百貫石，曲米麥各五十稱石，春衣羅五十匹，秋衣綾五十匹，春秋絹各二百匹，綿千兩。

translations.literal: Senior first rank: Three Preceptors — three hundred strings of cash and shi of grain, fifty shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, fifty bolts of silk gauze for spring garments, fifty bolts of damask for autumn garments, two hundred bolts of silk each for spring and autumn, one thousand liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Senior first rank — Three Preceptors: three hundred strings of cash and shi of grain; fifty measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; fifty bolts of silk gauze for spring and fifty of damask for autumn; two hundred bolts of silk each spring and autumn; one thousand liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 三公，錢粟二百五十貫石，曲米麥各四十稱石，春衣羅四十匹，秋衣綾四十匹，春秋絹各一百五十匹，綿七百兩。

translations.literal: Three Dukes — two hundred fifty strings of cash and shi of grain, forty shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, forty bolts of silk gauze for spring garments, forty bolts of damask for autumn garments, one hundred fifty bolts of silk each for spring and autumn, seven hundred liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Three Dukes: two hundred fifty strings of cash and shi of grain; forty measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; forty bolts of silk gauze for spring and forty of damask for autumn; one hundred fifty bolts of silk each spring and autumn; seven hundred liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 親王、尚書令，錢粟二百二十貫石，曲米麥各三十五稱石，春衣羅三十五匹，秋衣綾三十五匹，春秋絹各一百二十匹，綿六百兩。

translations.literal: Princes and Director of the Department — two hundred twenty strings of cash and shi of grain, thirty-five shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, thirty-five bolts of silk gauze for spring garments, thirty-five bolts of damask for autumn garments, one hundred twenty bolts of silk each for spring and autumn, six hundred liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and the Director of the Department: two hundred twenty strings of cash and shi of grain; thirty-five measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; thirty-five bolts of silk gauze for spring and thirty-five of damask for autumn; one hundred twenty bolts of silk each spring and autumn; six hundred liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，定制，皇兄弟及子封一字王者為親王，給二品俸，餘宗室封一字王者以三品俸給之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong, regulations were established: the emperor's brothers and sons enfeoffed as princes with single-character titles were made Princes and given second-rank salary; other members of the imperial clan enfeoffed as princes with single-character titles were given third-rank salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangtong (1142), regulations stipulated that the emperor's brothers and sons enfeoffed with single-character princely titles were made Princes and paid at second rank; other imperial clansmen with such titles were paid at third rank.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，以三師、宰臣以下有以一官而兼數職者，及有親王食其祿而複領他事者，前此並給以俸，今宜從一高，其兼職之俸並不重給。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande, because among the Three Preceptors, chief ministers, and below there were those who held one office while concurrently holding several posts, and there were princes who received their salary while also taking on other duties, previously all were given salary; now they should receive only the highest, and concurrent post salaries should not be given again.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiande (1150), because Three Preceptors, chief ministers, and others below them sometimes held multiple concurrent posts, and princes sometimes drew salary while also holding other offices, all had previously received full pay for each post. Henceforth only the highest salary applied; concurrent salaries were no longer paid twice.

sentences.zh: 至大定二十六年，詔有一官而兼數職，其兼職得罪亦不能免，而無廩給可乎。

translations.literal: By the twenty-sixth year of Dading, an edict stated: if one holds one office while concurrently holding several posts, when the concurrent post is punished for an offense one cannot be exempted — yet is it acceptable to receive no salary?
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Dading (1186), an edict observed that officials holding multiple concurrent posts could not escape punishment for offenses in any of those posts — yet should they receive no salary at all?

sentences.zh: 遂以職務煩簡定為分數，給兼職之俸。

translations.literal: Thereupon, according to whether duties were burdensome or simple, fractions were established and concurrent post salaries were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Salaries for concurrent posts were therefore set as fractional payments according to the relative burden of each duty.

sentences.zh: 從一品：左右丞相、都元帥、樞密使、郡王、開府儀同，錢粟二百貫石，曲米麥各三十稱石，春秋衣羅綾各三十匹，絹各一百匹，綿五百兩。

translations.literal: Junior first rank: Left and Right Chancellors, Grand Marshals, Privy Councilors, commandery princes, and Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness with the Same Privileges as a Prefectural Governor — two hundred strings of cash and shi of grain, thirty shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, thirty bolts each of silk gauze and damask for spring and autumn garments, one hundred bolts of silk each, five hundred liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Junior first rank — Left and Right Chancellors, Grand Marshals, Privy Councilors, commandery princes, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Prefectural-Governor Privileges: two hundred strings of cash and shi of grain; thirty measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; thirty bolts each of silk gauze and damask for spring and autumn; one hundred bolts of silk each season; five hundred liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 平章政事，錢粟一百九十貫石，曲米麥各二十八稱石，春羅秋綾各二十五匹，絹各九十五匹，綿四百五十兩。

translations.literal: Grand Councilors — one hundred ninety strings of cash and shi of grain, twenty-eight shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, twenty-five bolts of silk gauze for spring and twenty-five bolts of damask for autumn, ninety-five bolts of silk each, four hundred fifty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilors: one hundred ninety strings of cash and shi of grain; twenty-eight measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; twenty-five bolts of silk gauze for spring and twenty-five of damask for autumn; ninety-five bolts of silk each season; four hundred fifty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 大宗正，錢粟一百八十貫石，曲米麥各二十五稱石，羅綾同上，絹各九十匹，綿四百兩。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Clan — one hundred eighty strings of cash and shi of grain, twenty-five shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, silk gauze and damask the same as above, ninety bolts of silk each, four hundred liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Clan: one hundred eighty strings of cash and shi of grain; twenty-five measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; silk gauze and damask as above; ninety bolts of silk each season; four hundred liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 正二品：東宮三師、副元帥、左右丞，錢粟一百五十貫石。

translations.literal: Senior second rank: Three Preceptors of the Eastern Palace, Deputy Grand Marshals, and Left and Right Vice Chancellors — one hundred fifty strings of cash and shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Senior second rank — Three Preceptors of the Eastern Palace, Deputy Grand Marshals, and Left and Right Vice Chancellors: one hundred fifty strings of cash and shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 曲米麥各二十二稱石，春羅秋綾各二十二匹，絹各八十匹，綿三百五十兩。

translations.literal: Twenty-two shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, twenty-two bolts of silk gauze for spring and twenty-two bolts of damask for autumn, eighty bolts of silk each, three hundred fifty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; twenty-two bolts of silk gauze for spring and twenty-two of damask for autumn; eighty bolts of silk each season; three hundred fifty liang of cotton floss.

translations.literal: Junior second rank — one hundred forty strings of cash and shi of grain, twenty shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, twenty bolts of silk gauze for spring and twenty bolts of damask for autumn, seventy-five bolts of silk each, three hundred liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Junior second rank: one hundred forty strings of cash and shi of grain; twenty measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; twenty bolts of silk gauze for spring and twenty of damask for autumn; seventy-five bolts of silk each season; three hundred liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 同判大宗正，錢粟一百二十貫石，曲米麥各十八稱石，春羅秋綾各十八匹，絹各七十匹，綿二百五十兩。

translations.literal: Associate Director of the Imperial Clan — one hundred twenty strings of cash and shi of grain, eighteen shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, eighteen bolts of silk gauze for spring and eighteen bolts of damask for autumn, seventy bolts of silk each, two hundred fifty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Associate Director of the Imperial Clan: one hundred twenty strings of cash and shi of grain; eighteen measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; eighteen bolts of silk gauze for spring and eighteen of damask for autumn; seventy bolts of silk each season; two hundred fifty liang of cotton floss.

translations.literal: Senior third rank — seventy strings of cash and shi of grain, sixteen shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, twelve bolts of silk gauze for spring and twelve bolts of damask for autumn, fifty-five bolts of silk each, two hundred liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Senior third rank: seventy strings of cash and shi of grain; sixteen measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; twelve bolts of silk gauze for spring and twelve of damask for autumn; fifty-five bolts of silk each season; two hundred liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 外官，錢粟一百貫石，曲米麥各十五稱石，絹各四十匹，綿二百兩，公田三十頃。

translations.literal: External officials — one hundred strings of cash and shi of grain, fifteen shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, forty bolts of silk each, two hundred liang of cotton floss, thirty qing of official fields.
translations.idiomatic: External officials: one hundred strings of cash and shi of grain; fifteen measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; forty bolts of silk each season; two hundred liang of cotton floss; thirty qing of official fields.

sentences.zh: 統軍使、招討使、副使，錢粟八十貫石，曲米麥十三稱石，絹各三十五匹，綿百六十兩，公田二十五頃。

translations.literal: Regional Military Commanders, Pacification Commissioners, and deputy commissioners — eighty strings of cash and shi of grain, thirteen shi of fermented rice and wheat by measure, thirty-five bolts of silk each, one hundred sixty liang of cotton floss, twenty-five qing of official fields.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Military Commanders, Pacification Commissioners, and their deputies: eighty strings of cash and shi of grain; thirteen measured shi of fermented rice and wheat; thirty-five bolts of silk each season; one hundred sixty liang of cotton floss; twenty-five qing of official fields.

sentences.zh: 都運、府尹，錢粟七十貫石，曲米麥十二稱石，絹各三十匹，綿百四十兩。

translations.literal: Directors of Transport and Prefecture Governors — seventy strings of cash and shi of grain, twelve shi of fermented rice and wheat by measure, thirty bolts of silk each, one hundred forty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Directors of Transport and Prefecture Governors: seventy strings of cash and shi of grain; twelve measured shi of fermented rice and wheat; thirty bolts of silk each season; one hundred forty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，省奏：「職官公田歲入有數，前此百姓各隨公宇就輸，而吏或貪冒，多取以傷民。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande, the Secretariat memorialized: "The annual revenue of official fields for officeholders is fixed in amount; previously commoners each delivered payment at the official residence, but clerks sometimes were greedy and took more, harming the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiande (1150), the Secretariat memorialized: "The annual revenue from officials' public fields is fixed, but previously commoners delivered payments at each official's residence, and clerks sometimes extorted more than due, harming the people.

sentences.zh: 宜送之官倉，均定其數，與月俸隨給。」

translations.literal: It is appropriate to deliver it to government granaries, fix the amount uniformly, and distribute it along with monthly salary."
translations.idiomatic: Payments should be delivered to government granaries, the amounts standardized, and distributed along with monthly salaries."

sentences.zh: 從三品：錢粟六十貫石，曲米麥各十四稱石，春秋衣羅綾各十匹，絹各五十匹，綿百八十兩。

translations.literal: Junior third rank — sixty strings of cash and shi of grain, fourteen shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, ten bolts each of silk gauze and damask for spring and autumn garments, fifty bolts of silk each, one hundred eighty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Junior third rank: sixty strings of cash and shi of grain; fourteen measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; ten bolts each of silk gauze and damask for spring and autumn; fifty bolts of silk each season; one hundred eighty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 外官，錢粟六十貫石，曲米麥各十稱石，絹各二十五匹，綿一百二十兩，公田二十一頃。

translations.literal: External officials — sixty strings of cash and shi of grain, ten shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, twenty-five bolts of silk each, one hundred twenty liang of cotton floss, twenty-one qing of official fields.
translations.idiomatic: External officials: sixty strings of cash and shi of grain; ten measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; twenty-five bolts of silk each season; one hundred twenty liang of cotton floss; twenty-one qing of official fields.

sentences.zh: 皇統元年二月，詔諸官、職俱至三品而致仕者，俸祿、傔人，各給其半。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Huangtong, an edict stated that all officials whose offices all reached third rank and who retired received half their salary and half their attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Huangtong (1141), an edict stipulated that officials who retired while holding third rank or above received half their salary and half their allotted attendants.

sentences.zh: 正四品：錢粟四十五貫石，曲米麥各十二稱石，春秋衣羅綾各八匹，絹各四十匹，綿一百五十兩。

translations.idiomatic: Senior fourth rank: forty-five strings of cash and shi of grain; twelve measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; eight bolts each of silk gauze and damask for spring and autumn; forty bolts of silk each season; one hundred fifty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 外官，錢粟四十五貫石。

translations.literal: External officials — forty-five strings of cash and shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: External officials: forty-five strings of cash and shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 副統軍，錢粟五十貫石，絹各二十二匹，綿八十兩，職田十七頃。

translations.literal: Deputy Regional Military Commanders — fifty strings of cash and shi of grain, twenty-two bolts of silk each, eighty liang of cotton floss, seventeen qing of office fields.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Regional Military Commanders: fifty strings of cash and shi of grain; twenty-two bolts of silk each season; eighty liang of cotton floss; seventeen qing of office fields.

sentences.zh: 餘同下：曲米麥各八稱石，絹各二十匹，綿七十兩，公田十五頃，許帶酒三十瓶、鹽三石。

translations.literal: The rest the same as below: eight shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, twenty bolts of silk each, seventy liang of cotton floss, fifteen qing of official fields, permitted to carry thirty bottles of wine and three shi of salt.
translations.idiomatic: All other items as below: eight measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; twenty bolts of silk each season; seventy liang of cotton floss; fifteen qing of official fields; plus an allowance of thirty bottles of wine and three shi of salt.

sentences.zh: 從四品：錢粟四十貫石，曲麥米各十稱石，春秋羅綾各六匹，絹各三十匹，綿一百三十兩。

translations.literal: Junior fourth rank — forty strings of cash and shi of grain, ten shi each of fermented wheat and rice by measure, six bolts each of silk gauze and damask for spring and autumn, thirty bolts of silk each, one hundred thirty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Junior fourth rank: forty strings of cash and shi of grain; ten measured shi each of fermented wheat and rice; six bolts each of silk gauze and damask for spring and autumn; thirty bolts of silk each season; one hundred thirty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 外官，錢粟四十貫石，曲米麥各七稱石，絹各十八匹，綿六十兩，公田十四頃。

translations.literal: External officials — forty strings of cash and shi of grain, seven shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, eighteen bolts of silk each, sixty liang of cotton floss, fourteen qing of official fields.
translations.idiomatic: External officials: forty strings of cash and shi of grain; seven measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; eighteen bolts of silk each season; sixty liang of cotton floss; fourteen qing of official fields.

sentences.zh: 猛安，錢粟四十八貫石，餘皆無。

translations.literal: Meng'an — forty-eight strings of cash and shi of grain; all the rest none.
translations.idiomatic: Meng'an: forty-eight strings of cash and shi of grain; no other allowances.

sentences.zh: 烏魯古使，同，無職田。

translations.literal: Commissioner of Ulugu — the same; no office fields.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner of Ulugu: the same salary; no office fields.

sentences.zh: 大定二十年，詔猛安謀克俸給，令運司折支銀絹。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Dading, an edict on meng'an and mouke salaries ordered the transport offices to pay out silver and silk in commuted value.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Dading, an edict on meng'an and mouke salaries ordered transport offices to pay them in commuted silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 省臣議：「若估粟折支，各路運司儲積多寡不均，宜令依舊支請牛頭稅粟。

translations.literal: Provincial ministers deliberated: "If grain were commuted by valuation, the stores of transport offices in each route would be uneven in quantity; it is appropriate to order payment as before from the ox-head tax grain.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial ministers argued: "If salaries were commuted at grain valuations, transport-office reserves would vary unevenly across routes. Payment should continue as before from ox-head tax grain.

sentences.zh: 如遇凶年盡貸與民，其俸則于錢多路府支放，錢少則支銀絹亦未晚也。」

translations.literal: If in a famine year all is lent to the people, then the salary may be disbursed from route prefectures where cash is plentiful; where cash is scarce, paying silver and silk would not be too late either."
translations.idiomatic: If famine years require lending all grain to the people, salaries may be paid from route prefectures with ample cash; where cash is scarce, silver and silk payment would suffice."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

translations.idiomatic: Senior fifth rank: thirty-five strings of cash and shi of grain; eight measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; five bolts each of silk gauze and damask for spring and autumn; twenty-five bolts of silk each season; one hundred liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 外官，刺史、知軍、鹽使、錢粟三十五貫石，曲米麥各六稱石，絹各十七匹，綿五十五兩，公田十三頃。

translations.literal: External officials — Prefectural Governors, Military Commissioners, Salt Commissioners — thirty-five strings of cash and shi of grain, six shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, seventeen bolts of silk each, fifty-five liang of cotton floss, thirteen qing of official fields.
translations.idiomatic: External officials — Prefectural Governors, Military Commissioners, and Salt Commissioners: thirty-five strings of cash and shi of grain; six measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; seventeen bolts of silk each season; fifty-five liang of cotton floss; thirteen qing of official fields.

sentences.zh: 外官，錢粟二十五貫石，曲米麥各四稱石，絹各十匹，綿四十兩，公田七頃。

translations.literal: External officials — twenty-five strings of cash and shi of grain, four shi each of fermented rice and wheat by measure, ten bolts of silk each, forty liang of cotton floss, seven qing of official fields.
translations.idiomatic: External officials: twenty-five strings of cash and shi of grain; four measured shi each of fermented rice and wheat; ten bolts of silk each season; forty liang of cotton floss; seven qing of official fields.
