sentences.zh: 諸京作院都監、通州倉判、五品以上官司知法，錢粟九貫石，衣絹各二匹，綿六兩。

translations.literal: Various Capital workshop superintendents, Tongzhou Granary judges, legal clerks of bureaus of fifth rank and above — nine strings of cash and shi of grain, two bolts of garment silk each, six liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Capital workshop superintendents, Tongzhou Granary judges, and legal clerks of fifth-rank bureaus and above: nine strings of cash and shi of grain; two bolts of garment silk each season; six liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 諸府作院都監、諸埽物料場都監，錢粟八貫石，衣絹各一匹，綿六兩。

translations.literal: Various prefecture workshop superintendents and various embankment material yard superintendents — eight strings of cash and shi of grain, one bolt of garment silk each, six liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Prefecture workshop superintendents and embankment material yard superintendents: eight strings of cash and shi of grain; one bolt of garment silk each season; six liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 諸節鎮作院都監、諸司都監，錢粟八貫石，衣絹各二匹。

translations.literal: Various military-governorate workshop superintendents and various bureau superintendents — eight strings of cash and shi of grain, two bolts of garment silk each.
translations.idiomatic: Military-governorate workshop superintendents and bureau superintendents: eight strings of cash and shi of grain; two bolts of garment silk each season.

sentences.zh: 諸司同監，錢粟七貫石，絹同上。

translations.literal: Various bureau co-superintendents — seven strings of cash and shi of grain; silk the same as above.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau co-superintendents: seven strings of cash and shi of grain; silk as above.

sentences.zh: 陝西東路德順州世襲蕃巡檢，分例月支錢粟一十貫石，衣絹各二匹，綿一十兩。

translations.literal: Hereditary tribal patrol inspectors of Deshun Prefecture, Shaanxi East Route — by precedent, monthly payment of ten strings of cash and shi of grain, two bolts of garment silk each, ten liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary tribal patrol inspectors of Deshun Prefecture on the Shaanxi East Route received ten strings of cash and shi of grain monthly, two bolts of garment silk each season, and ten liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 陝西西路原州世襲蕃巡檢，月支錢二貫三百九十文，米四石五斗，絹三匹。

translations.literal: Hereditary tribal patrol inspectors of Yuan Prefecture, Shaanxi West Route — monthly payment of two strings three hundred ninety cash, four shi five dou of rice, three bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary tribal patrol inspectors of Yuan Prefecture on the Shaanxi West Route received two strings and three hundred ninety cash monthly, four shi and five dou of rice, and three bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 河東北路葭州等處世襲蕃巡檢，月支錢粟一十貫石，絹二匹，綿一十兩。

translations.literal: Hereditary tribal patrol inspectors of Jia Prefecture and elsewhere, Hedong North Route — monthly payment of ten strings of cash and shi of grain, two bolts of silk, ten liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary tribal patrol inspectors of Jia Prefecture and elsewhere on the Hedong North Route received ten strings of cash and shi of grain monthly, two bolts of silk, and ten liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 宮闈歲給。

translations.literal: Annual Allowances of the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Annual Inner-Palace Allowances.

sentences.zh: 太后、太妃宮，每歲各給錢二千萬，彩二百段，絹千匹，綿五千兩。

translations.literal: Palaces of the Empress Dowager and Grand Consorts — each year each was given twenty million cash, two hundred bolts of colored silk, one thousand bolts of silk, five thousand liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager's and Grand Consorts' palaces each received twenty million cash annually, two hundred bolts of colored silk, one thousand bolts of silk, and five thousand liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 諸妃，歲給錢千萬，彩百段，絹三百匹，綿三千兩。

translations.literal: Various consorts — annually given ten million cash, one hundred bolts of colored silk, three hundred bolts of silk, three thousand liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts received ten million cash annually, one hundred bolts of colored silk, three hundred bolts of silk, and three thousand liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 嬪以下，錢五百萬，彩五十段，絹二百匹，綿二千兩。

translations.literal: Imperial Concubines and below — five million cash, fifty bolts of colored silk, two hundred bolts of silk, two thousand liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Concubines and ranks below them received five million cash, fifty bolts of colored silk, two hundred bolts of silk, and two thousand liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，妃、嬪、婕妤、美人、及供膳女侍、並仙韶、長春院供應人等，歲給錢帛各有差。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, consorts, imperial concubines, talented ladies, beautiful ladies, and food-serving palace women, together with the Xian Shao and Changchun Court supply personnel and others, received annual cash and silk allowances of varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyuan, consorts, Imperial Concubines, Talented Ladies, Beautiful Ladies, food-serving palace women, and supply personnel of the Xian Shao and Changchun courts received annual cash and silk allowances at varying rates.

sentences.zh: 凡內職，貞祐之制，正一品，歲錢八千貫，幣百段，絹五百匹，綿五千兩。

translations.literal: For all inner-court offices, under the Zhenyou regulations: senior first rank — eight thousand strings of cash annually, one hundred bolts of ceremonial silk, five hundred bolts of silk, five thousand liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenyou regulations, inner-court offices at senior first rank received eight thousand strings of cash annually, one hundred bolts of ceremonial silk, five hundred bolts of silk, and five thousand liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 正二品，歲錢六千貫，幣八十段，絹三百匹，綿四千兩。

translations.literal: Senior second rank — six thousand strings of cash annually, eighty bolts of ceremonial silk, three hundred bolts of silk, four thousand liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Senior second rank: six thousand strings of cash annually, eighty bolts of ceremonial silk, three hundred bolts of silk, and four thousand liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 正三品，歲錢五千貫，幣六十段，絹二百匹，綿三千兩。

translations.literal: Senior third rank — five thousand strings of cash annually, sixty bolts of ceremonial silk, two hundred bolts of silk, three thousand liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Senior third rank: five thousand strings of cash annually, sixty bolts of ceremonial silk, two hundred bolts of silk, and three thousand liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 正四品，歲錢四千貫，幣四十段，絹百五十匹，綿二千兩。

translations.literal: Senior fourth rank — four thousand strings of cash annually, forty bolts of ceremonial silk, one hundred fifty bolts of silk, two thousand liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Senior fourth rank: four thousand strings of cash annually, forty bolts of ceremonial silk, one hundred fifty bolts of silk, and two thousand liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 正五品，尚宮夫人，歲錢二千貫，幣二十段，絹百匹，綿千兩。

translations.literal: Senior fifth rank — Ladies of the Palace Service Bureau: two thousand strings of cash annually, twenty bolts of ceremonial silk, one hundred bolts of silk, one thousand liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Senior fifth rank — Ladies of the Palace Service Bureau: two thousand strings of cash annually, twenty bolts of ceremonial silk, one hundred bolts of silk, and one thousand liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 尚宮左右夫人至宮正夫人，錢千五百貫，幣十九段，絹九十匹，綿九百兩。

translations.literal: Left and Right Ladies of the Palace Service Bureau through Chief Palace Ladies — one thousand five hundred strings of cash, nineteen bolts of ceremonial silk, ninety bolts of silk, nine hundred liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Ladies of the Palace Service Bureau through Chief Palace Ladies: one thousand five hundred strings of cash, nineteen bolts of ceremonial silk, ninety bolts of silk, and nine hundred liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 寶華夫人以下至資明夫人，錢千貫，幣十八段，絹八十匹，綿八百兩。

translations.literal: Treasured Splendor Lady and below through Graceful Wisdom Lady — one thousand strings of cash, eighteen bolts of ceremonial silk, eighty bolts of silk, eight hundred liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: From Treasured Splendor Lady through Graceful Wisdom Lady: one thousand strings of cash, eighteen bolts of ceremonial silk, eighty bolts of silk, and eight hundred liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 有大、小令人，大、小承禦，大、小近侍，俸各異。

translations.literal: There were Senior and Junior Attendants, Senior and Junior Imperial Attendants, Senior and Junior Close Attendants — salaries each differed.
translations.idiomatic: Senior and Junior Attendants, Senior and Junior Imperial Attendants, and Senior and Junior Close Attendants each received different salaries.

sentences.zh: 正六品，尚儀禦侍以下，錢五百貫，幣十六段，絹五十匹，綿二百兩。

translations.literal: Senior sixth rank — Palace Ceremonial Imperial Attendants and below: five hundred strings of cash, sixteen bolts of ceremonial silk, fifty bolts of silk, two hundred liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Senior sixth rank — Palace Ceremonial Imperial Attendants and below: five hundred strings of cash, sixteen bolts of ceremonial silk, fifty bolts of silk, and two hundred liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 正七品，司正禦侍以下，錢四百貫，幣十四段，絹四十匹，綿百五十兩。

translations.literal: Senior seventh rank — Chief Correctness Imperial Attendants and below: four hundred strings of cash, fourteen bolts of ceremonial silk, forty bolts of silk, one hundred fifty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Senior seventh rank — Chief Correctness Imperial Attendants and below: four hundred strings of cash, fourteen bolts of ceremonial silk, forty bolts of silk, and one hundred fifty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 正八品，典儀禦侍以下，錢三百貫，幣十二段，絹三十匹，綿百兩。

translations.literal: Senior eighth rank — Ceremonial Imperial Attendants and below: three hundred strings of cash, twelve bolts of ceremonial silk, thirty bolts of silk, one hundred liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Senior eighth rank — Ceremonial Imperial Attendants and below: three hundred strings of cash, twelve bolts of ceremonial silk, thirty bolts of silk, and one hundred liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 正九品，掌儀禦侍以下，錢二百五十貫，幣十段，絹二十六匹，綿百兩。

translations.literal: Senior ninth rank — Managing Ceremonial Imperial Attendants and below: two hundred fifty strings of cash, ten bolts of ceremonial silk, twenty-six bolts of silk, one hundred liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ninth rank — Managing Ceremonial Imperial Attendants and below: two hundred fifty strings of cash, ten bolts of ceremonial silk, twenty-six bolts of silk, and one hundred liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 百司承應俸給。

translations.literal: Salaries of Attendants in the Hundred Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Salaries of Bureau Attendants.

sentences.zh: 省令史、譯史、錢粟一十貫石，絹四匹，綿四十兩。

translations.literal: Secretariat clerks and translators — ten strings of cash and shi of grain, four bolts of silk, forty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat clerks and translators: ten strings of cash and shi of grain, four bolts of silk, and forty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 省通事、樞密令史譯史，錢粟十二貫石，絹三匹，綿三十兩。

translations.literal: Secretariat interpreters and Privy Council clerks and translators — twelve strings of cash and shi of grain, three bolts of silk, thirty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat interpreters and Privy Council clerks and translators: twelve strings of cash and shi of grain, three bolts of silk, and thirty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 樞密通事、六部御史台令譯史，錢粟一十貫石，衣絹三匹，綿三十兩。

translations.literal: Privy Council interpreters, Six Ministries and Censorate clerks and translators — ten strings of cash and shi of grain, three bolts of garment silk, thirty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Council interpreters and Six Ministries/Censorate clerks and translators: ten strings of cash and shi of grain, three bolts of garment silk, and thirty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 六部等通事、誥院令史、國史院書寫、隨府書表、親王府祗候郎君、典客署引接書表，錢粟八貫石，絹二匹，綿二十兩。

translations.literal: Six Ministries and other interpreters, Patent Office clerks, National History Academy scribes, Prefecture memorial scribes, Princely Residence attendant gentlemen, Reception Office memorial guides — eight strings of cash and shi of grain, two bolts of silk, twenty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Six Ministries interpreters, Patent Office clerks, National History Academy scribes, prefecture memorial scribes, Princely Residence attendant gentlemen, and Reception Office memorial guides: eight strings of cash and shi of grain, two bolts of silk, and twenty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 走馬郎君、一品子孫十貫石，內祗八貫石，班祗七貫石，並絹二匹，綿二十兩。

translations.literal: Mounted courier gentlemen and first-rank descendants — ten strings of cash and shi of grain; inner attendants — eight strings; roster attendants — seven strings; all with two bolts of silk and twenty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Mounted courier gentlemen and first-rank descendants received ten strings of cash and shi of grain; inner attendants eight strings; roster attendants seven strings; all with two bolts of silk and twenty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 護衛長，支正六品俸。

translations.literal: Guard captains — paid senior sixth-rank salary.
translations.idiomatic: Guard captains were paid at senior sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 長行，從六品俸。

translations.literal: Regular guards — junior sixth-rank salary.
translations.idiomatic: Regular guards were paid at junior sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎、奉禦、東宮護衛長，錢粟十七貫石，絹八匹，綿四十兩。

translations.literal: Tally and Seal Gentlemen, Imperial Attendants, Eastern Palace Guard captains — seventeen strings of cash and shi of grain, eight bolts of silk, forty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Tally and Seal Gentlemen, Imperial Attendants, and Eastern Palace Guard captains: seventeen strings of cash and shi of grain, eight bolts of silk, and forty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 東宮護衛長行，十五貫石，絹四匹，綿四十兩。

translations.literal: Eastern Palace Guard regulars — fifteen strings of cash and shi of grain, four bolts of silk, forty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Palace Guard regulars: fifteen strings of cash and shi of grain, four bolts of silk, and forty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 筆硯承奉、閣門祗候、侍衛親軍百戶，十二貫石，絹四匹，綿三十兩。

translations.literal: Inkstone attendants, Gate attendants, Personal Guard company commanders — twelve strings of cash and shi of grain, four bolts of silk, thirty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Inkstone attendants, Gate attendants, and Personal Guard company commanders: twelve strings of cash and shi of grain, four bolts of silk, and thirty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 妃護衛、奉職、符寶典書、東宮入殿小底，十貫石，絹三匹，綿三十兩，勒留則添二貫石。

translations.literal: Consort guards, Service Attendants, Tally and Seal recorders, Eastern Palace inner-hall attendants — ten strings of cash and shi of grain, three bolts of silk, thirty liang of cotton floss; if retained by order, two additional strings of cash and shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Consort guards, Service Attendants, Tally and Seal recorders, and Eastern Palace inner-hall attendants: ten strings of cash and shi of grain, three bolts of silk, and thirty liang of cotton floss; two additional strings if retained by order.

sentences.zh: 尚衣、奉禦、捧案、擎執、奉輦、知把書畫、隨庫本把、左右藏庫本把、儀鸞局本把、尚輦局本把、妃奉事，八貫石，絹三匹，綿三十兩。

translations.literal: Palace Wardrobe attendants, Imperial Attendants, tray-bearers, standard-bearers, palanquin attendants, painting and calligraphy custodians, warehouse custodians, Left and Right Treasury custodians, Ceremonial Guard custodians, Palanquin Bureau custodians, consort attendants — eight strings of cash and shi of grain, three bolts of silk, thirty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Wardrobe attendants, Imperial Attendants, tray-bearers, standard-bearers, palanquin attendants, painting/calligraphy custodians, warehouse and treasury custodians, Ceremonial Guard and Palanquin Bureau custodians, and consort attendants: eight strings of cash and shi of grain, three bolts of silk, and thirty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 侍衛親軍五十戶，九貫石，絹三匹，綿三十兩。

translations.literal: Personal Guard fifty-household commanders — nine strings of cash and shi of grain, three bolts of silk, thirty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Personal Guard fifty-household commanders: nine strings of cash and shi of grain, three bolts of silk, and thirty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 未系班，絹三匹，綿二十兩。

translations.literal: Not yet placed on the roster — three bolts of silk, twenty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Those not yet placed on the roster received three bolts of silk and twenty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 長行，七貫石，絹二匹，綿二十兩。

translations.literal: Regular guards — seven strings of cash and shi of grain, two bolts of silk, twenty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Regular guards: seven strings of cash and shi of grain, two bolts of silk, and twenty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 弩傘什將，八貫石。

translations.literal: Crossbow and umbrella squad commanders — eight strings of cash and shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Crossbow and umbrella squad commanders: eight strings of cash and shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 傘子，五貫石。

translations.literal: Umbrella bearers — five strings of cash and shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Umbrella bearers: five strings of cash and shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 太醫長行，八貫石，正奉上太醫，十貫石。

translations.literal: Imperial Medical regular attendants — eight strings of cash and shi of grain; Chief Attending Imperial Physicians — ten strings of cash and shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Medical regular attendants received eight strings of cash and shi of grain; Chief Attending Imperial Physicians received ten strings.

sentences.zh: 副奉上，同。

translations.literal: Deputy Attending — the same.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Attending Physicians received the same.

sentences.zh: 隨位承應都監，未及十五歲者六貫石，從八品七貫石，從七品八貫石，從六品九貫石，從五品十貫石，從四品十二貫石，止掌文書者添支三貫石，牌子頭等添支二貫石。

translations.literal: Rank-attendant chief superintendents — those not yet fifteen years old six strings of cash and shi of grain; junior eighth rank seven strings; junior seventh rank eight strings; junior sixth rank nine strings; junior fifth rank ten strings; junior fourth rank twelve strings; those handling documents only received an additional three strings of cash and shi of grain; tally chiefs and the like received an additional two strings of cash and shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Rank-attendant chief superintendents under fifteen received six strings of cash and shi of grain; junior eighth rank seven strings; junior seventh rank eight; junior sixth rank nine; junior fifth rank ten; junior fourth rank twelve. Those handling documents only received three additional strings; tally chiefs and the like received two additional strings.

sentences.zh: 司天四科人，九品六貫石，八品七貫石，六品九貫石，五品十貫石，四品十二貫石，止教授管勾十貫石，學生錢三貫、米五斗。

translations.literal: Personnel of the four categories in the Bureau of Astronomy — ninth rank six strings of cash and shi of grain, eighth rank seven strings, sixth rank nine strings, fifth rank ten strings, fourth rank twelve strings; instructors and supervisors only ten strings of cash and shi of grain; students three strings of cash and five dou of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau of Astronomy personnel in four categories: ninth rank six strings of cash and shi of grain; eighth rank seven; sixth rank nine; fifth rank ten; fourth rank twelve. Instructors and supervisors received ten strings only. Students received three strings of cash and five dou of rice.

sentences.zh: 典客、書表，八貫石，絹二匹，綿二十兩。

translations.literal: Reception Office and memorial scribes — eight strings of cash and shi of grain, two bolts of silk, twenty liang of cotton floss.
translations.idiomatic: Reception Office attendants and memorial scribes: eight strings of cash and shi of grain, two bolts of silk, and twenty liang of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 東宮筆硯，六貫石。

translations.literal: Eastern Palace inkstone attendants — six strings of cash and shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Palace inkstone attendants: six strings of cash and shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 尚廄獸醫，秘書監楷書，六貫石。

translations.literal: Imperial Stud veterinarians and Secretariat regular-script copyists — six strings of cash and shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Stud veterinarians and Secretariat regular-script copyists: six strings of cash and shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 秘書琴棋等待詔，七貫石。

translations.literal: Secretariat zither, chess, and other attendants awaiting edict — seven strings of cash and shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat zither, chess, and other attendants awaiting imperial summons: seven strings of cash and shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 駝馬牛羊群子、擠酪人，皆三貫石。

translations.literal: Camel, horse, cattle, and sheep herd keepers and cheese makers — all three strings of cash and shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Keepers of camel, horse, cattle, and sheep herds and cheese makers all received three strings of cash and shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 諸使司都監食直，二十萬貫以上六十貫，十萬貫已上五十貫，五萬貫已上四十貫，三萬貫已上三十貫，二萬貫已上二十五貫。

translations.literal: Commission allowances for superintendents of the various commissioner offices — two hundred thousand strings and above sixty strings, one hundred thousand strings and above fifty strings, fifty thousand strings and above forty strings, thirty thousand strings and above thirty strings, twenty thousand strings and above twenty-five strings.
translations.idiomatic: Commission allowances for superintendents of commissioner offices: sixty strings for revenues of two hundred thousand strings or more; fifty for one hundred thousand or more; forty for fifty thousand or more; thirty for thirty thousand or more; twenty-five for twenty thousand or more.

sentences.zh: 諸院務監官食直，五千貫已上監官二十貫、同監十五貫，二千貫已上監官十五貫、同監十貫，一千貫已上監官十五貫，一千貫已下監官十貫。

translations.literal: Commission allowances for superintendents of the various bureaus and works — five thousand strings and above: superintendent twenty strings, co-superintendent fifteen strings; two thousand strings and above: superintendent fifteen strings, co-superintendent ten strings; one thousand strings and above: superintendent fifteen strings; below one thousand strings: superintendent ten strings.
translations.idiomatic: Commission allowances for bureau superintendents: for revenues of five thousand strings or more, the superintendent received twenty strings and the co-superintendent fifteen; at two thousand or more, fifteen and ten; at one thousand or more, fifteen for the superintendent alone; below one thousand, ten for the superintendent.

sentences.zh: 舊制，凡監臨使司、院務之商稅，增者有賞，虧者克俸。

translations.literal: Under the old system, for all commercial taxes supervised by commissioner offices and bureaus, increases brought rewards and deficits brought salary deductions.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, supervisors of commercial taxes at commissioner offices and bureaus were rewarded for increases and had their salaries reduced for shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 大定九年，上以吏非祿無以養廉，於是止增虧分數為殿最，乃罷克俸、給賞之制，而監官酬賞仍舊。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dading, the emperor said that officials without salary could not maintain integrity; thereupon surplus and deficit amounts alone were used for merit ratings, the systems of salary deduction and reward payment were abolished, but superintendent rewards remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Dading (1169), the emperor observed that officials could not remain upright without adequate salary. Surplus and deficit figures were thereafter used only for merit ratings; salary deductions and reward payments were abolished, though superintendent bonuses continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 二十年，詔十萬貫以上鹽酒等使，若虧額五厘，克俸一分。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, an edict stated that for salt, wine, and similar commissioners with revenues of one hundred thousand strings and above, if the deficit reached five li, one fen of salary was deducted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (1180), an edict stipulated that salt, wine, and similar commissioners with revenues of one hundred thousand strings or more would have one tenth of their salary deducted for every half-percent shortfall.

sentences.zh: 奏隨處提點院務官賞格，其省除以上提點官、並運司親管院務，若能增者十分為率以六分入官，二分與提點所官、二分與監官充賞，若虧亦依此例克俸，若能足數則全給。

translations.literal: A memorial fixed the reward scale for bureau superintendents everywhere: for provincially appointed supervising officials and bureaus directly managed by transport offices, if revenue increased, taking ten parts as the standard, six parts entered the treasury, two parts went to supervising officials of the office, and two parts served as reward for superintendents; if there was deficit, salary was deducted by the same rule; if the quota was met, payment was made in full.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial established reward scales for bureau superintendents throughout the realm. For provincially appointed supervisors and bureaus directly managed by transport offices, surpluses were divided ten ways: six parts to the treasury, two to supervising officials, and two as bonuses for superintendents. Deficits were penalized proportionally; meeting the quota brought full payment.

sentences.zh: 大定二十二年，定每月先支其半外，如不虧則全支，虧一分則克其一分，補足貼支。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Dading, it was fixed that each month half was paid first; if there was no deficit the remainder was paid in full; for each one fen of deficit one fen was deducted; when made up, the balance was paid supplementally.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Dading (1182), the rule was set that half the monthly salary was paid in advance; if there was no shortfall the balance was paid in full, but each tenth of deficit reduced payment by a tenth, with the remainder paid once the shortfall was made up.

sentences.zh: 隨路使司、院務並坊場，例多虧課。

translations.literal: Route commissioner offices, bureaus, and market stalls mostly had revenue deficits as a rule.
translations.idiomatic: Route commissioner offices, bureaus, and market stalls routinely fell short of their revenue quotas.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「若其實可減處，約量裁減，亦公私兩便也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If there are places where reduction is truly possible, estimate and trim accordingly — that would benefit both public and private interests alike."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Where quotas can genuinely be lowered, they should be trimmed to fit circumstances. That would serve both the state and the people."

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以省除提控官、與運司置司處，虧課一分克俸一分，其罰涉重。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, because provincially appointed supervising officials and places where transport offices maintained offices had one fen of revenue deficit met with one fen of salary deduction, the penalty was excessively heavy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year (1183), the rule that provincially appointed supervisors and transport-office posts lose one tenth of salary for every tenth of revenue shortfall was judged excessively harsh.

sentences.zh: 亦命先給月俸之半，餘半驗所虧分數克罰補，公田則不在克限。

translations.literal: It was also ordered that half the monthly salary be paid first, and the remaining half verified against the amount of deficit for deduction or supplemental payment; official fields were not within the limits of deduction.
translations.idiomatic: It was also ordered that half the monthly salary be paid in advance, with the remainder adjusted according to the shortfall; income from official fields was exempt from such deductions.

sentences.zh: 二十六年四月，奏定院務監官虧永陪償格。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-sixth year, a memorial fixed the scale for permanent compensation by bureau superintendents for deficits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-sixth year (1186), a memorial established the permanent compensation scale for bureau superintendents liable for revenue deficits.

sentences.zh: 諸京府運司提刑司節鎮防刺等，漢人、女直、契丹司吏、譯史、通史、孔目官，八貫。

translations.literal: At all capital prefectures, transport offices, judicial commissioner offices, military prefectures, garrison prefectures, and the like — Han, Jurchen, and Khitan clerks, translators, record keepers, and case officers — eight strings.
translations.idiomatic: At capital prefectures, transport offices, judicial commissioner offices, military prefectures, and garrison prefectures, Han, Jurchen, and Khitan clerks, translators, record keepers, and case officers received eight strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 押司官，七貫。

translations.literal: Chief clerks — seven strings.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerks received seven strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 前後行，六貫。

translations.literal: Front and rear runners — six strings.
translations.idiomatic: Front and rear runners received six strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 諸防刺已上女直、契丹司吏、譯史、通事，不問千里內外，錢七貫，公田三頃。

translations.literal: At all garrison prefectures and above, Jurchen and Khitan clerks, translators, and interpreters — regardless of whether within or beyond one thousand li — seven strings of cash and three qing of official fields.
translations.idiomatic: At garrison prefectures and above, Jurchen and Khitan clerks, translators, and interpreters received seven strings of cash and three qing of official fields, regardless of distance within or beyond one thousand li.

sentences.zh: 諸鹽使司都目，十四貫。

translations.literal: Chief clerks of all salt commissioner offices — fourteen strings.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerks of salt commissioner offices received fourteen strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 司吏，六貫。

translations.literal: Clerks — six strings.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks received six strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 諸巡院司縣司獄等司吏，有譯史，通事者同，錢五貫。

translations.literal: Clerks of patrol offices, county offices, prisons, and the like — those with translators or interpreters the same — five strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks of patrol offices, county offices, and prisons, including those serving as translators or interpreters, received five strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 凡諸吏人，月支大紙五十張，小紙五百張，筆二管、墨二錠。

translations.literal: For all clerical personnel, monthly issue was fifty large sheets of paper, five hundred small sheets, two brushes, and two cakes of ink.
translations.idiomatic: All clerical personnel received monthly supplies of fifty large sheets of paper, five hundred small sheets, two brushes, and two cakes of ink.

sentences.zh: 諸職官上任，不過初二日，罷任過初五日者，給當月俸。

translations.literal: For all officeholders taking office no later than the second day of the month, or leaving office after the fifth day, the salary for that month was paid.
translations.idiomatic: Officeholders who assumed office by the second of the month, or who left office after the fifth, received the full salary for that month.

sentences.zh: 或受差及因公幹未能之官者，計程外聽給到任祿。

translations.literal: If one received a dispatch or, because of official business, was unable to reach one's post, beyond the travel time salary upon arrival was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: If an appointee was dispatched but delayed by official business, salary was paid from the time of arrival, excluding travel days.

sentences.zh: 若文牒未至，前官在任，及後官已到，前官差出，其祿兩支，職田皆給後官。

translations.literal: If documents had not yet arrived and the predecessor remained in office, or if the successor had already arrived and the predecessor was dispatched elsewhere, both received salary, but office fields were all given to the successor.
translations.idiomatic: If appointment documents had not yet arrived and the predecessor remained in office, or if the successor had arrived while the predecessor was dispatched elsewhere, both received salary, but office fields went entirely to the successor.

sentences.zh: 凡職田，畝取粟三斗、草一稱。

translations.literal: For all office fields, three dou of grain and one bundle of fodder were taken per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Office fields yielded three dou of grain and one bundle of fodder per mu.

sentences.zh: 倉場隨月俸支俸，曲則隨直折價。

translations.literal: Granaries paid salary along with monthly salary; fermented grain was commuted at direct valuation.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries disbursed salary with the monthly payment; fermented grain was paid at commuted value.

sentences.zh: 諸親王授任者，祿從多，職田從職。

translations.literal: For all princes upon appointment, salary followed the higher amount and office fields followed the actual office.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed princes received the higher of applicable salaries and office fields according to their actual posts.

sentences.zh: 朝官兼外者同。

translations.literal: Court officials concurrently holding external posts — the same.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials holding concurrent external posts followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 六十以上及未六十而病致仕者，給其祿半。

translations.literal: Those sixty and above, and those who retired due to illness before sixty, received half their salary.
translations.idiomatic: Officials sixty or older, and those who retired due to illness before reaching sixty, received half salary.

sentences.zh: 承應及軍功初出職未曆致仕，雖未六十者亦給半祿。

translations.literal: Attendants and those whose first appointment came through military merit who retired without having served through office, even if not yet sixty, also received half salary.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants and those first appointed through military merit who retired without full service, even if under sixty, also received half salary.

sentences.zh: 內外吏員及諸局分承應人，病告至百日則停給。

translations.literal: Internal and external clerical staff and attendants in the various bureaus — if sick leave reached one hundred days, payment ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Internal and external clerks and bureau attendants on sick leave for one hundred days ceased to receive payment.

sentences.zh: 除程給假者俸祿職田皆以半給，衣絹則全給。

translations.literal: Except for travel leave, salary, emoluments, and office fields were all paid at half; garment silk was paid in full.
translations.idiomatic: Except during authorized travel leave, salary and office-field income were paid at half rate, but garment silk was paid in full.

sentences.zh: 皇家袒免以上親戶別給。

translations.literal: Imperial kin of the tanmian degree of mourning and above received separate household allowances.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial relatives within the tanmian degree of mourning and above received separate household allowances.

sentences.zh: 夫亡，妻亦同。

translations.literal: If the husband died, the wife received the same.
translations.idiomatic: If the husband died, the wife received the same allowance.

sentences.zh: 若同居兄弟收充猛安謀克及歷任承應人者，不在給限。

translations.literal: If co-residing brothers were enrolled as meng'an or mouke, or had served as attendants, they were not within the limits of payment.
translations.idiomatic: Co-residing brothers enrolled as meng'an or mouke, or who had served as attendants, were excluded from these allowances.

sentences.zh: 大功以上，錢粟一十三貫石，春秋衣絹各四匹。

translations.literal: For greater merit mourning and above — thirteen strings of cash and shi of grain, four bolts of garment silk each for spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives in greater-merit mourning and above received thirteen strings of cash and shi of grain, plus four bolts of garment silk each for spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 小功，粟一十貫石，春秋衣絹各三匹。

translations.literal: Lesser merit mourning — ten strings of cash and shi of grain, three bolts of garment silk each for spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives in lesser-merit mourning received ten strings of cash and shi of grain, plus three bolts of garment silk each for spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 緦麻、袒免，錢粟八貫石，春秋衣絹二匹。

translations.literal: Fine hemp and tanmian mourning — eight strings of cash and shi of grain, two bolts of garment silk for spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives in fine-hemp and tanmian mourning received eight strings of cash and shi of grain and two bolts of garment silk for spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 諸馳驛及長行馬，職官日給。

translations.literal: For all postal relay and long-distance travel horses, officeholders received daily allowances.
translations.idiomatic: Officeholders on postal relay or long-distance travel received daily allowances.

sentences.zh: 謂奉宣省院台部委差、或許差者，下文置所等官同。

translations.literal: This means those dispatched by the Secretariat, Privy Council, and Censorate on imperial commission, or those permitted dispatch; downstream placement-office officials were the same.
translations.idiomatic: This applied to officials dispatched by the Secretariat, Privy Council, or Censorate on imperial commission, or those specially authorized to travel, as well as officials at downstream placement offices.

sentences.zh: 一品三貫文，二品二貫文，三品一貫五百文，四品一貫二百文，五品一貫文，六品八百文，七百六百文，八品九品四百文。

translations.literal: First rank three strings of cash, second rank two strings, third rank one string five hundred cash, fourth rank one string two hundred cash, fifth rank one string, sixth rank eight hundred cash, seventh rank six hundred cash, eighth and ninth ranks four hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: First rank three strings of cash; second rank two strings; third rank one string five hundred cash; fourth rank one string two hundred cash; fifth rank one string; sixth rank eight hundred cash; seventh rank six hundred cash; eighth and ninth ranks four hundred cash.

sentences.zh: 有職事官日給，外路官往回口券，依上款給一品二貫五百文，二品一貫六百文，三品一貫二百文，四品一貫文，五品九百文，六品七百文，七品六百文，八品九品四百文。

translations.literal: Officeholders with active posts received daily allowances; external-route officials received round-trip travel ration coupons paid according to the preceding scale: first rank two strings five hundred cash, second rank one string six hundred cash, third rank one string two hundred cash, fourth rank one string, fifth rank nine hundred cash, sixth rank seven hundred cash, seventh rank six hundred cash, eighth and ninth ranks four hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: Active officeholders received daily allowances. External-route officials received round-trip travel ration coupons at the following rates: first rank two strings five hundred cash; second rank one string six hundred cash; third rank one string two hundred cash; fourth rank one string; fifth rank nine hundred cash; sixth rank seven hundred cash; seventh rank six hundred cash; eighth and ninth ranks four hundred cash.

sentences.zh: 無職事官並驗前職日給，無前職者以應仕及待闕職事給之。

translations.literal: Those without active posts were all paid daily allowances according to their former offices; those without former offices were paid according to eligible or pending offices.
translations.idiomatic: Officials without active posts received daily allowances based on their former rank; those without former rank were paid according to their eligible or pending appointment.

sentences.zh: 四品一貫三百文，五品一貫二百文，六品九百文，七品七百文，八品九品五百文。

translations.literal: Fourth rank one string three hundred cash, fifth rank one string two hundred cash, sixth rank nine hundred cash, seventh rank seven hundred cash, eighth and ninth ranks five hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank one string three hundred cash; fifth rank one string two hundred cash; sixth rank nine hundred cash; seventh rank seven hundred cash; eighth and ninth ranks five hundred cash.

sentences.zh: 隨朝吏員宣差及省部差委官踏逐者，引者亦同。

translations.literal: Court clerks on imperial dispatch and officials commissioned by provincial ministries who escorted them — guides were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Court clerks on imperial dispatch and officials commissioned by provincial ministries to escort them received the same allowance, as did their guides.

sentences.zh: 及統軍司按察司書吏譯人、本局差委及隨逐者，日給錢各一百五十文。

translations.literal: Regional Military and Investigation commissioner clerks and translators, those commissioned by their own bureaus, and those who escorted them — each received one hundred fifty cash daily.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Military and Investigation commissioner clerks and translators, bureau appointees, and their escorts each received one hundred fifty cash per day.

sentences.zh: 燕賜各部官僚以下，日給米糧分例，無草地處內，親王給馬二十五匹草料，親王米一石，宰執七斗，王府三斗，府尉二斗，員外郎、司馬各一斗六升，監察御史、尚書省都事、大理司直、六部主事各八升，檢、知法七升，省令、譯史六升，院台令譯史，省通事各五升，院台通事、六部令譯史通事、省祗候郎君、使庫都監各四升，誥院令史、樞密院移剌各三升，王府直府、王府及省知印直省、御史台通引、王府教讀、王傅府尉等下司吏、外路通事、省醫工調角匠、招討司移剌各二升、寫誥諸祗候人本破人同、大程官院子酒匠柴火各一升，萬戶一斗六升，猛安八升，謀克四升，蒲輦二升，正軍阿裏喜，旗鼓吹笛司吏各一升。

translations.literal: At banquet grants for officials of the various ministries and below, daily grain allotments were fixed; where there was no pastureland, princes were given fodder for twenty-five horses; princes one shi of rice, chief ministers seven dou, princely households three dou, household commandants two dou, vice directors and marshals one dou six sheng each, investigating censors, Secretariat chief clerks, Court of Judicial Review direct examiners, and Six Ministries section chiefs eight sheng each, inspectors and legal officers seven sheng, Secretariat clerks and translators six sheng, Privy Council and Censorate clerks and translators and Secretariat interpreters five sheng each, Privy Council and Censorate interpreters, Six Ministries clerks, translators, and interpreters, Secretariat attendant gentlemen, and treasury superintendents four sheng each, Patent Office clerks and Privy Council yila three sheng each, princely household direct stewards, princely household and Secretariat seal keepers and direct secretariat staff, Censorate guides, princely tutors and household commandants and subordinate clerks, external-route interpreters, Secretariat medical workers and horn craftsmen, Pacification Commission yila two sheng each, Patent scribes and various attendants and regular provision staff the same, chief route officials, courtyard wine makers, and firewood handlers one sheng each, wanhu one dou six sheng, meng'an eight sheng, mouke four sheng, puyan two sheng, regular soldiers and Ali Xi, banner, drum, pipe, and flute bureau clerks one sheng each.
translations.idiomatic: At imperial banquets, daily grain allotments were fixed for officials of the ministries and below. Where pasture was unavailable, princes received fodder for twenty-five horses. Princes received one shi of rice; chief ministers seven dou; princely households three dou; household commandants two dou; vice directors and marshals one dou six sheng each; investigating censors, Secretariat chief clerks, Court of Judicial Review direct examiners, and Six Ministries section chiefs eight sheng each; inspectors and legal officers seven sheng; Secretariat clerks and translators six sheng; Privy Council and Censorate clerks and translators and Secretariat interpreters five sheng each; Privy Council and Censorate interpreters, Six Ministries clerks, translators, and interpreters, Secretariat attendant gentlemen, and treasury superintendents four sheng each; Patent Office clerks and Privy Council yila three sheng each; princely household stewards, princely and Secretariat seal keepers, Censorate guides, princely tutors, subordinate clerks, external-route interpreters, Secretariat medical workers and horn craftsmen, and Pacification Commission yila two sheng each; patent scribes, attendants, and regular provision staff the same; chief route officials, courtyard wine makers, and firewood handlers one sheng each; wanhu one dou six sheng; meng'an eight sheng; mouke four sheng; puyan two sheng; regular soldiers and Ali Xi, and banner, drum, pipe, and flute bureau clerks one sheng each.

sentences.zh: 諸外方進貢及回賜、並人使長行馬，每匹日給草一稱、粟一斗。

translations.literal: For all external tribute missions and return gifts, and envoy long-distance travel horses, each horse daily received one bundle of fodder and one dou of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Horses on external tribute missions, return-gift missions, and envoy travel received one bundle of fodder and one dou of grain per horse per day.

sentences.zh: 宮中東宮同承應人因公差出，皆驗見請錢粟貫石、口給食料，若系本職者住程不在給限，其常破馬草料局分，如被差長行馬公幹本支草料，即聽驗日克除，若特奉宣差勾當者，依本格。

translations.literal: Palace and Eastern Palace attendants alike, when dispatched on official business, all had verified current cash-and-grain entitlements and received daily food allowances; if the stopover was part of inherent duty it was not within the payment limit; for bureaus that regularly supplied horse fodder, if a long-distance horse on official business used its regular fodder allowance, daily deduction was permitted upon verification; if specially dispatched on imperial commission, the standard scale applied.
translations.idiomatic: Palace and Eastern Palace attendants dispatched on official business received daily food allowances according to their verified cash-and-grain entitlements. Stopovers inherent to their duties were not counted. Where a bureau normally supplied horse fodder and a long-distance horse on official business drew its regular allowance, the days could be deducted accordingly; special imperial commissions followed the standard scale.

sentences.zh: 十八貫石以上九百文，十七貫石八百六十文，十五貫石以上五百四十文，七貫石以上四百六十文，六貫石四百二十文，五貫石三百八十文，四貫石三百三十文，三貫石二百八十文，二貫石二百三十文。

translations.literal: Eighteen strings of cash and shi of grain and above nine hundred cash, seventeen strings eight hundred sixty cash, fifteen strings and above five hundred forty cash, seven strings and above four hundred sixty cash, six strings four hundred twenty cash, five strings three hundred eighty cash, four strings three hundred thirty cash, three strings two hundred eighty cash, two strings two hundred thirty cash.
translations.idiomatic: Daily food allowances by salary level: eighteen strings of cash and shi of grain or above, nine hundred cash; seventeen strings, eight hundred sixty cash; fifteen strings or above, five hundred forty cash; seven strings or above, four hundred sixty cash; six strings, four hundred twenty cash; five strings, three hundred eighty cash; four strings, three hundred thirty cash; three strings, two hundred eighty cash; two strings, two hundred thirty cash.

sentences.zh: 諸試護衛親軍，聽自起發日為始，計程至都，比至試補，其間各日給口券，若揀退還家者，亦驗回程給之。

translations.literal: For all trial Personal Guard conscripts, counting from the day of departure to the capital until trial appointment, daily travel ration coupons were given for each day in between; if rejected and sent home, the return journey was also paid upon verification.
translations.idiomatic: Trial Personal Guard conscripts received daily travel ration coupons from the day of departure until trial appointment in the capital; those rejected and sent home received the same for the return journey.

sentences.zh: 未起閑住口數不在支限。

translations.literal: Days of idle lodging before departure were not within the payment limit.
translations.idiomatic: Days spent idle before departure were not counted toward travel allowances.

sentences.zh: 其正收之後再揀退者，亦給人三口米糧錢一百文、馬二匹草料。

translations.literal: Those formally accepted and then rejected again were also given grain and cash for three persons at one hundred cash, and fodder for two horses.
translations.idiomatic: Those formally accepted and then rejected again also received grain and cash for three persons at one hundred cash, plus fodder for two horses.

sentences.zh: 諸簽軍赴鎮防處、及班祗充押遞橫差別路勾當千里以上者，沿路各日給米一升、馬一匹草料。

translations.literal: For all enlisted soldiers proceeding to garrison posts, and roster attendants serving as relay escorts on cross-route business of one thousand li or more, each day along the route one sheng of rice and fodder for one horse were given.
translations.idiomatic: Enlisted soldiers proceeding to garrison posts, and roster attendants on relay escort duty for cross-route business of one thousand li or more, received one sheng of rice and fodder for one horse per day along the route.

sentences.zh: 無馬有驢者，各支依本格。

translations.literal: Those without horses but with donkeys — each was paid according to the standard scale.
translations.idiomatic: Those without horses but with donkeys were paid according to the standard scale.

sentences.zh: 車駕巡幸，顧工，馬夫三百文，步夫二百三十文，圍鵝夫，隨程幹辦人各二百文，傳遞果子夫一百五十文。

translations.literal: On imperial tours, hired laborers — horse handlers three hundred cash, foot carriers two hundred thirty cash, goose-enclosure handlers, route attendants two hundred cash each, relay fruit carriers one hundred fifty cash.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours, hired laborers were paid as follows: horse handlers three hundred cash; foot carriers two hundred thirty cash; goose-enclosure handlers and route attendants two hundred cash each; relay fruit carriers one hundred fifty cash.

sentences.zh: 車駕巡幸，若於私家內安置行宮者，約量給賜段匹。

translations.literal: On imperial tours, if a temporary palace was established within a private residence, cloth gifts were given in estimated measure.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial tour established a temporary palace in a private residence, cloth gifts were awarded in appropriate measure.

sentences.zh: 太廟神廚祠祭度勾當人、少府監隨色工匠、部役官受給官司吏，錢粟二貫石，春秋衣絹各一匹。

translations.literal: Imperial Temple kitchen sacrifice handlers, Palace Workshop artisans by specialty, department conscript officials receiving salary, and bureau clerks — two strings of cash and shi of grain, one bolt of garment silk each for spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Temple kitchen sacrifice handlers, Palace Workshop artisans by specialty, department conscript officials on salary, and bureau clerks received two strings of cash and shi of grain, plus one bolt of garment silk each for spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 諸局作匠人請俸，繡女都管錢粟五貫石，都繡頭錢粟四貫石，副繡頭三貫五百石，中等細繡人三貫石，次等細繡人二貫五百石，習學本把正辦人錢支次等之半，描繡五人錢粟三貫石，司吏二人三貫石。

translations.literal: Salaries requested by craftsmen in the various bureau workshops — chief embroidery supervisors five strings of cash and shi of grain, chief embroidery heads four strings, deputy embroidery heads three strings five hundred cash, mid-grade fine embroiderers three strings, lower-grade fine embroiderers two strings five hundred cash, apprentices, foremen, and regular handlers received half the lower grade; five pattern embroiderers three strings of cash and shi of grain; two clerks three strings of cash and shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Salaries for craftsmen in bureau workshops: chief embroidery supervisors five strings of cash and shi of grain; chief embroidery heads four strings; deputy embroidery heads three strings five hundred cash; mid-grade fine embroiderers three strings; lower-grade fine embroiderers two strings five hundred cash; apprentices, foremen, and regular handlers half the lower grade; five pattern embroiderers three strings of cash and shi of grain; two clerks three strings of cash and shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 修內司，作頭五貫石，工匠四貫石，春秋衣絹各二匹。

translations.literal: Palace Construction Office — foremen five strings of cash and shi of grain, craftsmen four strings, two bolts of garment silk each for spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Construction Office foremen received five strings of cash and shi of grain; craftsmen four strings; both received two bolts of garment silk each for spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 軍夫除錢糧外，日支錢五十，米一升半。

translations.literal: Military corvée laborers, besides regular cash and grain pay, received fifty cash daily and one and a half sheng of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Military corvée laborers, in addition to their regular cash and grain pay, received fifty cash and one and a half sheng of rice per day.

sentences.zh: 百姓夫每日支錢一百、米一升半。

translations.literal: Commoner corvée laborers daily received one hundred cash and one and a half sheng of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Commoner corvée laborers received one hundred cash and one and a half sheng of rice per day.

sentences.zh: 國子監雕字匠人，作頭六貫石，副作頭四貫石，春秋衣絹各二匹。

translations.literal: National University engraving craftsmen — foremen six strings of cash and shi of grain, deputy foremen four strings, two bolts of garment silk each for spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: National University engraving craftsmen: foremen six strings of cash and shi of grain; deputy foremen four strings; both received two bolts of garment silk each for spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 長行三貫石，射糧軍匠錢粟三貫石，春秋衣絹各二匹，習學給半。

translations.literal: Regular guards three strings of cash and shi of grain; grain-provision military craftsmen three strings of cash and shi of grain, two bolts of garment silk each for spring and autumn; apprentices received half.
translations.idiomatic: Regular guards received three strings of cash and shi of grain; grain-provision military craftsmen three strings of cash and shi of grain and two bolts of garment silk each for spring and autumn; apprentices received half pay.

sentences.zh: 初習學匠錢六百，米六斗，春秋絹各一匹，布各一匹。

translations.literal: Beginning apprentice craftsmen — six hundred cash, six dou of rice, one bolt of silk each for spring and autumn, one bolt of cloth each.
translations.idiomatic: Beginning apprentice craftsmen received six hundred cash, six dou of rice, one bolt of silk each for spring and autumn, and one bolt of cloth each.

sentences.zh: 民匠日支錢一百八十文。

translations.literal: Civilian craftsmen daily received one hundred eighty cash.
translations.idiomatic: Civilian craftsmen received one hundred eighty cash per day.

sentences.zh: 諸隨朝五品以下職事官身故，因公差出、及以理去任、未給解由者，身故同。

translations.literal: For all court officeholders of fifth rank and below who died in office — whether on official dispatch, or who left office legitimately without having received a certificate of release — death was treated the same.
translations.idiomatic: Court officeholders of fifth rank and below who died in office — whether on official dispatch, or who had left office legitimately without receiving a certificate of release — were treated the same for funeral allowances.

sentences.zh: 驗品，從去鄉地裏支給津遣錢。

translations.literal: Rank was verified, and funeral travel allowance was paid according to the distance from one's native place.
translations.idiomatic: Rank was verified and funeral travel allowance paid according to the distance from the deceased's native place.

sentences.zh: 並受職事給之，下條承應人准此。

translations.literal: All were paid according to the office held; attendants in the section below followed this rule.
translations.idiomatic: Payment followed the office held; attendants covered in the next section followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 若外路官員在任依理身故者，皆依上官品地裏減半給之。

translations.literal: If external-route officials died in office legitimately, all were paid at half according to the superior official's rank and native distance.
translations.idiomatic: External-route officials who died legitimately in office received half the allowance calculated by the superior official's rank and native distance.

sentences.zh: 若系五百里內不在給限，五百裏外，五品一百貫，六品七品八十貫，八品九品六十貫。

translations.literal: If within five hundred li, payment was not within the limit; beyond five hundred li — fifth rank one hundred strings, sixth and seventh ranks eighty strings, eighth and ninth ranks sixty strings.
translations.idiomatic: Within five hundred li no allowance was paid. Beyond five hundred li: fifth rank one hundred strings; sixth and seventh ranks eighty strings; eighth and ninth ranks sixty strings.

sentences.zh: 一千裏外，五品一百二十貫，六品七品一百貫，八品九品八十貫。

translations.literal: Beyond one thousand li — fifth rank one hundred twenty strings, sixth and seventh ranks one hundred strings, eighth and ninth ranks eighty strings.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond one thousand li: fifth rank one hundred twenty strings; sixth and seventh ranks one hundred strings; eighth and ninth ranks eighty strings.

sentences.zh: 二千裏外，五品一百七十貫，六品七品一百五十貫，八品九品一百貫。

translations.literal: Beyond two thousand li — fifth rank one hundred seventy strings, sixth and seventh ranks one hundred fifty strings, eighth and ninth ranks one hundred strings.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond two thousand li: fifth rank one hundred seventy strings; sixth and seventh ranks one hundred fifty strings; eighth and ninth ranks one hundred strings.

sentences.zh: 三千裏外，五品二百五十貫，六品七品二百貫，八品九品一百五十貫。

translations.literal: Beyond three thousand li — fifth rank two hundred fifty strings, sixth and seventh ranks two hundred strings, eighth and ninth ranks one hundred fifty strings.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond three thousand li: fifth rank two hundred fifty strings; sixth and seventh ranks two hundred strings; eighth and ninth ranks one hundred fifty strings.

sentences.zh: 諸隨朝承應人身故應給津遣錢者，護衛東宮護衛同、奉禦、符寶、都省樞密院御史台令譯史同九品官，通事、宗正府六部令譯史、統軍司書史譯書、按察司書史，同。

translations.literal: For all court attendants entitled to funeral travel allowance upon death — Personal Guard and Eastern Palace Guard the same; Imperial Attendants, Tally and Seal Gentlemen, and clerks and translators of the central ministries, Privy Council, and Censorate the same as ninth-rank officials; interpreters, Imperial Clan Court and Six Ministries clerks and translators, Regional Military commissioner clerks, translators, and scribes, and Investigation commissioner clerks — the same.
translations.idiomatic: Court attendants entitled to funeral travel allowance: Personal Guard and Eastern Palace Guard the same; Imperial Attendants, Tally and Seal Gentlemen, and central ministry, Privy Council, and Censorate clerks and translators at ninth-rank rates; interpreters, Imperial Clan Court and Six Ministries clerks and translators, Regional Military commissioner clerks, translators, and scribes, and Investigation commissioner clerks the same.

sentences.zh: 親軍減九品官五分之二，通事、隨朝書表、吏員、譯人、統軍司通事、守當官，按察司書吏、譯人，分治都水監典吏，同。

translations.literal: Personal Guard — reduced two-fifths from the ninth-rank official rate; interpreters, court memorial scribes, clerical staff, translators, Regional Military commissioner interpreters, gate keepers, Investigation commissioner clerks and translators, and capital Waterworks Bureau clerks — the same.
translations.idiomatic: Personal Guard received two-fifths less than ninth-rank officials; interpreters, court memorial scribes, clerical staff, translators, Regional Military commissioner interpreters, gate keepers, Investigation commissioner clerks and translators, and capital Waterworks Bureau clerks the same.

sentences.zh: 及諸局分承應人武衛軍同減五分之三。

translations.literal: And attendants in the various bureaus and Martial Guard — the same, reduced three-fifths.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants in the various bureaus and Martial Guard received three-fifths less.

sentences.zh: 天壽節設施老疾貧民錢數，在都七百貫宮籍監給，諸京二十五貫此以下並系省錢給，諸府二十貫文，諸節鎮一十五貫文，諸防刺州軍一十貫文，諸外縣五貫文。

translations.literal: Funds distributed on the TianShou Festival for the aged, sick, and poor — in the capital seven hundred strings from the Palace Registry Office; all capitals twenty-five strings, below that all from provincial funds; all prefectures twenty strings of cash; all military prefectures fifteen strings of cash; all garrison prefectures and armies ten strings of cash; all outer counties five strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshou Festival charity for the aged, sick, and poor: seven hundred strings in the capital from the Palace Registry Office; twenty-five strings in each capital, with lower amounts from provincial funds; twenty strings in prefectures; fifteen in military prefectures; ten in garrison prefectures and armies; five in outer counties.

sentences.zh: 城寨系保鎮同。

translations.literal: Fortified posts and protected towns — the same.
translations.idiomatic: Fortified posts and protected towns followed the same scale.

sentences.zh: 諸孤老幼疾人，各月給米二斗、錢五百文，春秋衣絹各一匹五歲以下三分給二，身死者給錢一貫埋殯。

translations.literal: For all orphaned aged and sick persons, each month two dou of rice and five hundred cash were given; one bolt of garment silk each for spring and autumn; those under five years old received two-thirds; upon death one string of cash was given for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned aged and infirm persons received two dou of rice and five hundred cash monthly, plus one bolt of garment silk each for spring and autumn; children under five received two-thirds; upon death one string of cash was provided for burial.

sentences.zh: 諸因災傷或遭賊驚卻饑荒去處，良民典顧、冒賣為驅，遇恩官贖為良分例若元價錢給，男子一十五貫文，婦人同，老幼各減半。

translations.literal: In all places where, because of disaster or alarm from bandits followed by famine, commoners had pawned themselves or falsely sold themselves as slaves, upon encountering an amnesty officials redeemed them as commoners at the standard rate of the original price — men fifteen strings of cash, women the same, old and young each at half.
translations.idiomatic: Where disaster, bandit raids, or famine had driven commoners to pawn or sell themselves into servitude, amnesties authorized officials to redeem them at standard rates: fifteen strings of cash for men and women alike, half that for the old and young.

sentences.zh: 六歲以下即聽出離，不在贖換之限。

translations.literal: Those under six years old were permitted to leave the household immediately and were not within the limits of redemption.
translations.idiomatic: Children under six could leave the household immediately and were exempt from redemption requirements.

sentences.zh: 諸士庶陳言利害，若有可采，行之便於官民者，依驗等第給賞，上等銀絹三十兩匹，中等二十兩匹，下等一十兩匹，其陳數事，止從一支。

translations.literal: For all scholars and commoners who submitted proposals on public interest, if there was something adoptable and implementing it would benefit officials and commoners alike, rewards were given according to verified grade — upper grade thirty taels of silver and bolts of silk, middle grade twenty taels and bolts, lower grade ten taels and bolts; if several matters were submitted, only one reward was given.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and commoners who submitted useful proposals benefiting both state and people received graded rewards: upper grade thirty taels of silver and bolts of silk; middle grade twenty; lower grade ten. Multiple submissions received only one reward.

sentences.zh: 若用大事應補官者，從吏部格。

translations.literal: If a major matter warranted appointment to office, the regulations of the Ministry of Personnel were followed.
translations.idiomatic: If a proposal involved a major matter warranting official appointment, Ministry of Personnel regulations applied.

sentences.zh: 宣宗貞祐元年十二月，以糧儲不足，詔隨朝官、承應人俸，計口給之，餘依市直折之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Zhenyou under Emperor Xuanzong, because grain stores were insufficient, an edict stated that salaries for court officials and attendants were to be paid by mouth count, with the remainder commuted at market value.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Zhenyou (1213), grain stores proving insufficient, an edict ordered court officials' and attendants' salaries paid per capita, with the remainder commuted at market rates.

sentences.zh: 諭旨省臣曰：「聞親軍俸，粟每石以麥六斗折之，所省能幾，而失眾心，令給本色。」

translations.literal: An edict instructed the provincial ministers: "I have heard that for Personal Guard salaries, each shi of grain is commuted to six dou of wheat — how much can be saved, yet hearts are lost; order payment in kind."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed the provincial ministers: "I hear Personal Guard salaries are paid with six dou of wheat commuted for each shi of grain. The savings are trifling, yet morale suffers. Order payment in kind."

sentences.zh: 二年八月，始給京府州縣及轉運司吏人月俸有差。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year, differentiated monthly salaries began to be paid to clerical staff of capital prefectures, counties, and transport offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year (1214), differentiated monthly salaries were introduced for clerical staff in capital prefectures, counties, and transport offices.

sentences.zh: 舊制惟吏案孔目官有俸，餘止給食錢，故更定焉。

translations.literal: Under the old system only case-office chief clerks had salary; the rest received only food money — hence the reform.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system only chief case clerks received salary; others received only food allowances — hence the reform.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔損宮中諸位歲給有差。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict reduced the annual grants of the various palace households with differences.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1215), an edict reduced annual grants to the various palace households on a graded basis.

sentences.zh: 監察御史田迥秀言：「國家調度，行才數月，已後停滯，所患在支太多，收太少，若隨時裁損所支，而增其收，庶可久也。」

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Tian Huixiu said: "The state's fiscal arrangements operate for only a few months before stagnating afterward; the trouble lies in expenditure too great and revenue too little; if expenditure is trimmed in timely fashion and revenue increased, perhaps it can last."
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Tian Huixiu said: "State finances run for only a few months before stalling. Expenditure is too great and revenue too small. If spending is trimmed in timely fashion and collections increased, the treasury may endure."

sentences.zh: 因條五事：「一曰朝官及令譯史、諸司吏員、諸局承應人，太冗濫宜省並之。

translations.literal: He then listed five items: "First, court officials and clerks and translators, clerical staff of the various offices, and attendants of the various bureaus are excessively numerous and redundant — they should be reduced and consolidated.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed five measures: "First, court officials, clerks and translators, office clerical staff, and bureau attendants are excessively numerous and should be consolidated.

sentences.zh: 隨處屯軍皆設寄治官，徒費俸給，不若令有司兼總之。

translations.literal: Garrison armies everywhere have nominal officials posted separately — they waste salary for nothing; it would be better to let responsible offices manage them concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison armies everywhere maintain nominal separate officials who waste salary to no purpose; responsible offices should manage them concurrently instead.

sentences.zh: 且沿河亭障各駐鄉兵，彼皆白徒，皆不可用，不若以此軍代之，以省其出。」

translations.literal: Moreover, along the river fortifications local militia are garrisoned at each post — they are all raw recruits and all unusable; it would be better to replace them with these armies and thereby save expenditure."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, local militia garrison the riverine fortifications — raw recruits, all unusable. These garrison troops should replace them and save the expense."

sentences.zh: 四月，以調度不及，罷隨朝六品以下官及承應人從己人力輸傭錢。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, because finances could not keep pace, the personal-servant corvée money paid by court officials of sixth rank and below and attendants was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, finances failing to keep pace, the corvée money for personal servants of court officials sixth rank and below and their attendants was abolished.

sentences.zh: 減修內司所役軍夫之半。

translations.literal: The military corvée laborers employed by the Palace Construction Office were reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: Military corvée labor assigned to the Palace Construction Office was cut by half.

sentences.zh: 經兵處，州、府、司吏減半，司、縣三分減一，其餘除開封府、南京轉運司外，例減三分之一。

translations.literal: In areas that had experienced warfare, prefecture and commissioner office clerks were reduced by half; circuit and county offices by one-third; all the rest, except Kaifeng Prefecture and the Southern Capital Transport Office, were uniformly reduced by one-third.
translations.idiomatic: In war-affected areas, prefecture and commissioner office clerks had their pay cut by half; circuit and county offices by one-third; everywhere else, except Kaifeng Prefecture and the Southern Capital Transport Office, pay was cut by one-third across the board.

sentences.zh: 有祿官吏而不出境者，並罷給券，出境者給其半。

translations.literal: Salaried officials who did not leave their jurisdiction had all travel vouchers cancelled; those who left received half.
translations.idiomatic: Salaried officials who remained within their jurisdiction ceased to receive travel vouchers; those who traveled abroad received half the usual allowance.

sentences.zh: 興定二年正月，詔：「陝州等處司、縣官徵稅不足，閣其俸給何以養廉，自今不復閣俸。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Xingding, an edict stated: "At Shaanzhou and elsewhere, when circuit and county officials' tax collection fell short, withholding their salaries — how could they maintain integrity? From now on salaries will no longer be withheld."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Xingding, an edict declared: "At Shaanzhou and elsewhere, when circuit and county officials failed to meet tax quotas, withholding their salaries undermined their integrity. Henceforth salaries will no longer be withheld.

sentences.zh: 彰化軍節度使張行信言：「送宣之使，其視五品而上各有定數，後竟停罷。

translations.literal: Military Governor of Zhanghua Zhang Xingxin said: "Envoys bearing imperial decrees — those of fifth rank and above each had fixed quotas, but this was later suspended altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Military Governor of Zhanghua Zhang Xingxin memorialized: "Envoys bearing imperial decrees once received fixed allowances according to rank for those of fifth rank and above, but this practice was later abolished.

sentences.zh: 今軍官以上奉待使者有所饋獻，至六品以下亦不免如例，而莫能辦，則斂所部以與之，至有獲罪者。

translations.literal: Now military officers and above, when entertaining envoys, make gifts; even those of sixth rank and below cannot avoid the custom, and when unable to afford it they levy from their subordinates to give gifts, some even suffering punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Now military officers and above are expected to offer gifts when entertaining envoys, and even sixth rank and below cannot escape the custom. When they cannot afford it, they levy their subordinates to make the gifts — some have even been punished for this.

sentences.zh: 保舉縣尹，特增其俸，然法行至今，而關以西尚有未到任者，豈所舉少而不敷耶？

translations.literal: When nominating county magistrates, their salaries were specially increased; yet the policy has been in effect until now, and west of the passes there are still those who have not taken up office — is it because too few were nominated and the numbers do not suffice?
translations.idiomatic: Nominated county magistrates received specially increased salaries, yet even now positions west of the passes remain unfilled. Were too few candidates nominated to meet the need?

sentences.zh: 宜廣選舉，以補其闕。

translations.literal: Broader selection should be made to fill the vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: Broader recruitment should be undertaken to fill these vacancies.

sentences.zh: 且丞簿亦親民者也，而獨不增，安能禁其侵牟哉！」

translations.literal: Moreover, assistant magistrates and registrars also serve the people directly, yet their salaries alone were not increased — how can their extortion be prevented!"
translations.idiomatic: Assistant magistrates and registrars also serve the people directly, yet their salaries alone were not raised. How can we prevent them from preying on the populace?"
